187.title: Murder defined
187.plain: Murder is the unlawful killing of a human being, or a fetus, with malice aforethought; this section sets no penalty.
acts: the unlawful killing of a human being, or a fetus

188.title: Malice defined
188.plain: Defines express and implied malice for murder and says no other mental state need be shown once an intentional act with malice is shown.

189.title: Degrees of murder
189.plain: Murder by listed means or during listed felonies, or by willful, deliberate, premeditated killing, is first degree; all other murder is second degree. This section sets no penalty.
acts: All murder that is perpetrated by means of a destructive device or explosive
All other kinds of murders

189.1.title: Peace officer murder declaration
189.1.plain: States the Legislature's finding that willful, deliberate, premeditated killing of a peace officer is first degree murder and that the section declares existing law.

189.5.title: Burden of proof in murder trial
189.5.plain: Places on the defendant the burden of proving mitigation, justification or excuse once the killing is proved at a murder trial.

190.title: Punishment for murder
190.plain: First degree murder is punished by death, life without parole, or 25 years to life; second degree murder by 15 years to life, with longer terms when a peace officer is killed.
acts: Every person guilty of murder in the first degree

190.03.title: Hate crime first degree murder
190.03.plain: First-degree murder that is a hate crime is punished by life in state prison without the possibility of parole.
acts: commits first-degree murder that is a hate crime

190.05.title: Second degree murder after prior murder term
190.05.plain: A person guilty of second degree murder who served a prior prison term for murder gets life without parole or 15 years to life.
acts: found guilty of murder in the second degree

190.1.title: Phases of capital trial
190.1.plain: Requires a case in which the death penalty may be imposed to be tried in separate phases: guilt, special circumstances, sanity, then penalty.

190.2.title: Special circumstances murder penalty
190.2.plain: First degree murder with a listed special circumstance is punished by death or life in prison without parole; aiders with intent to kill, and certain major participants, face the same penalty.
acts: Every person, not the actual killer, who, with the intent to kill, aids, abets, counsels, commands, induces, solicits, requests, or assists any actor in the commission of murder in the first degree

190.25.title: Murder of transit worker
190.25.plain: First degree murder of an on-duty transit driver or ticket agent, with a special circumstance found true, is punished by life in prison without parole, including for intentional aiders.
acts: Every person whether or not the actual killer found guilty of intentionally aiding, abetting, counseling, commanding, inducing, soliciting, requesting, or assisting any actor in the commission of murder in the first degree

190.3.title: Penalty phase of capital case
190.3.plain: Sets how the trier of fact decides between death and life without parole, including the evidence and factors considered.

190.4.title: Special circumstance findings
190.4.plain: Sets procedures for finding special circumstances, the penalty hearing, and review of a death verdict.

190.41.title: Corpus delicti in felony special circumstances
190.41.plain: Says the corpus delicti of a felony-based special circumstance need not be proved independently of the defendant's extrajudicial statement.

190.5.title: Murder by a minor, penalty limits
190.5.plain: Death cannot be imposed on a person under 18; a 16- or 17-year-old guilty of special circumstances first degree murder gets life without parole or, at the court's discretion, 25 years to life.
acts: guilty of murder in the first degree

190.6.title: Expediting capital appeals
190.6.plain: Declares legislative goals and time limits for briefing and deciding appeals in death penalty cases.

190.7.title: Record in capital appeals
190.7.plain: Defines what the entire record on appeal includes in a death penalty case.

190.8.title: Certifying capital case record
190.8.plain: Sets deadlines and duties for certifying the record on appeal where a death sentence has been imposed.

190.9.title: Reporting in capital cases
190.9.plain: Requires all superior court proceedings in a possible death penalty case to be reported and transcribed.

191.title: Petit treason abolished
191.plain: Abolishes the common-law rules of petit treason, making those killings ordinary homicides.

191.5.title: Vehicular manslaughter while intoxicated
191.5.plain: Killing a person while driving in violation of listed Vehicle Code intoxication sections is gross vehicular manslaughter (4 to 10 years) or vehicular manslaughter while intoxicated (up to 4 years); repeat offenders face 15 years to life.
acts: the unlawful killing of a human being without malice aforethought, in the driving of a vehicle

192.title: Manslaughter defined
192.plain: Manslaughter is the unlawful killing of a human being without malice: voluntary, involuntary, or vehicular. This section sets no penalty.
acts: the unlawful killing of a human being without malice

192.5.title: Vehicular manslaughter in a vessel
192.5.plain: Unlawfully killing a person without malice while operating a vessel is vehicular manslaughter; fleeing the scene adds five years in state prison.
acts: Operating a vessel in the commission of an unlawful act, not amounting to a felony, and with gross negligence

193.title: Punishment for manslaughter
193.plain: Voluntary manslaughter carries 3, 6, or 11 years in state prison; involuntary manslaughter and vehicular manslaughter carry lower or alternative terms set out by type.
acts: A violation of paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 192
A violation of paragraph (2) of subdivision (c) of Section 192
A violation of paragraph (3) of subdivision (c) of Section 192

193.5.title: Punishment for vessel manslaughter
193.5.plain: Sets penalties for manslaughter committed while operating a vessel, from up to one year in county jail to 4, 6, or 10 years in state prison.
acts: A violation of subdivision (a) of Section 192.5
A violation of subdivision (b) of Section 192.5
A violation of subdivision (c) of Section 192.5
A violation of subdivision (d) of Section 192.5

193.7.title: Habitual traffic offender designation
193.7.plain: Designates a person convicted of vehicular manslaughter while intoxicated with two or more recent Vehicle Code violations as a habitual traffic offender for three years.

193.8.title: Lending vehicle to intoxicated minor
193.8.plain: An adult who lets an intoxicated minor drive their vehicle, where the minor is later convicted of a listed offense, faces a fine up to $1,000 or up to six months in county jail.
acts: shall not relinquish possession of the vehicle to a minor for the purpose of driving

194.title: Death after three years and a day
194.plain: Says death need not occur within three years and a day for a killing to be murder or manslaughter, but later death raises a rebuttable presumption the killing was not criminal.

195.title: Excusable homicide
195.plain: Lists the cases in which a homicide is excusable.

196.title: Justifiable homicide by peace officers
196.plain: Lists the circumstances in which homicide by peace officers and those aiding them is justifiable.

197.title: Justifiable homicide
197.plain: Lists the cases in which a homicide is justifiable, such as resisting an attempt to murder or to commit a felony, or defending habitation, property, or person.

198.title: Fear needed to justify homicide
198.plain: Says a bare fear of the offenses in subdivisions 2 and 3 of Section 197 is not enough; the circumstances must excite the fears of a reasonable person.

198.5.title: Presumed fear when force used at home
198.5.plain: Creates a presumption of reasonable fear when force likely to cause death or great bodily injury is used against an unlawful and forcible entrant into one's residence, and defines great bodily injury.

199.title: Acquittal when homicide justifiable
199.plain: Says that when a homicide appears justifiable or excusable, the person indicted must be fully acquitted and discharged at trial.

203.title: Mayhem defined
203.plain: Mayhem is unlawfully and maliciously depriving a person of a body member or disabling, disfiguring, or rendering it useless; this section states no penalty.
acts: deprives a human being of a member of his body, or disables, disfigures, or renders it useless, or cuts or disables the tongue, or puts out an eye, or slits the nose, ear, or lip

204.title: Punishment for mayhem
204.plain: Mayhem is punishable by imprisonment in the state prison for two, four, or eight years.
acts: Mayhem

205.title: Aggravated mayhem
205.plain: Aggravated mayhem is intentionally causing permanent disability or disfigurement, or depriving a person of a limb, organ, or member, with extreme indifference; it is punishable by life in state prison with the possibility of parole.
acts: intentionally causes permanent disability or disfigurement of another human being or deprives a human being of a limb, organ, or member of his or her body

206.title: Torture
206.plain: Torture is inflicting great bodily injury on another with intent to cause cruel or extreme pain and suffering for revenge, extortion, persuasion, or a sadistic purpose; this section states no penalty.
acts: inflicts great bodily injury as defined in Section 12022.7 upon the person of another

206.1.title: Punishment for torture
206.1.plain: Torture is punishable by life in state prison, with parole eligibility only after at least seven years, or ten years in the stated case involving a child 14 or younger.
acts: torture

207.title: Kidnapping
207.plain: Kidnapping is forcibly or by fear taking or holding a person and carrying them elsewhere, enticing a child under 14, or bringing a person into the state; this section states no penalty.
acts: steals or takes, or holds, detains, or arrests any person in this state, and carries the person into another country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county

hires, persuades, entices, decoys, or seduces by false promises, misrepresentations, or the like, any child under the age of 14 years to go out of this country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county
takes or holds, detains, or arrests any person, with a design to take the person out of this state
abducts or takes by force or fraud any person contrary to the law of the place where that act is committed, and brings, sends, or conveys that person within the limits of this state

208.title: Punishment for kidnapping
208.plain: Kidnapping is punishable by three, five, or eight years in state prison, or five, eight, or eleven years if the victim is under 14; probation requires 12 months in county jail except in unusual cases.
acts: Kidnapping

209.title: Kidnapping for ransom or to commit a crime
209.plain: Kidnapping for ransom, reward, or extortion is a felony punishable by life, without parole if the victim dies or is harmed; kidnapping to commit robbery or a sex offense is life with parole.
acts: seizes, confines, inveigles, entices, decoys, abducts, conceals, kidnaps, or carries away another person by any means whatsoever with intent to hold or detain, or who holds or detains, that person for ransom, reward, or to commit extortion or to exact from another person any money or valuable thing, or a person who aids or abets any such act
kidnaps or carries away an individual to commit robbery, rape, oral copulation, sodomy, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, 289, or former Section 262

209.5.title: Kidnapping during a carjacking
209.5.plain: Kidnapping another person during a carjacking to facilitate it is punishable by life in state prison with the possibility of parole.
acts: kidnaps another person who is not a principal in the commission of the carjacking

210.title: Posing as kidnapper for ransom
210.plain: Posing as a kidnapper, or as someone able to obtain a victim's release, to obtain ransom, reward, or money is a felony punishable by imprisonment for two, three, or four years.
acts: poses as, or in any manner represents himself to be a person who has seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped or carried away any person

210.5.title: False imprisonment as shield or to avoid arrest
210.5.plain: False imprisonment of a person to protect against arrest, substantially increasing risk of harm, or to use as a shield, is punishable under subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for three, five, or eight years.
acts: commits the offense of false imprisonment, as defined in Section 236, against a person

211.title: Robbery
211.plain: Robbery is the felonious taking of personal property from another's person or immediate presence, against their will, by force or fear; this section states no penalty.
acts: taking of personal property in the possession of another, from his person or immediate presence, and against his will, accomplished by means of force or fear

212.title: Fear in robbery
212.plain: Says the fear mentioned in Section 211 may be fear of unlawful injury to the person robbed or relatives, or of immediate unlawful injury to anyone in the person robbed's company.

212.5.title: Degrees of robbery
212.5.plain: Sets which robberies are of the first degree, such as those of transit operators and passengers, in inhabited dwellings, or at automated teller machines, and says all others are second degree.

213.title: Punishment for robbery
213.plain: Robbery of the first degree carries three to nine years in state prison depending on the case, and second degree carries two, three, or five years.
acts: Robbery of the first degree
Robbery of the second degree
attempted robbery in violation of paragraph (2) of subdivision (a)

214.title: Train robbery and train interference
214.plain: Boarding a train to rob passengers, or interfering with railroad track, signals, or trains with intent to rob, is a felony; this section states no term.
acts: goes upon or boards any railroad train, car or engine
interferes in any manner with any switch, rail, sleeper, viaduct, culvert, embankment, structure or appliance pertaining to or connected with any railroad
places any dynamite or other explosive substance or material upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle
stops any such train, car or engine, or slackens the speed thereof

215.title: Carjacking
215.plain: Carjacking is the felonious taking of a motor vehicle from another's person or immediate presence by force or fear; it is punishable by three, five, or nine years in state prison.
acts: taking of a motor vehicle in the possession of another, from his or her person or immediate presence, or from the person or immediate presence of a passenger of the motor vehicle, against his or her will

217.1.title: Assault on public officials
217.1.plain: Assaulting listed officials such as judges, prosecutors, or peace officers in retaliation for or to prevent official duties is a wobbler; attempted murder of them carries 15 years to life.
acts: commits any assault upon the President or Vice President of the United States
attempts to commit murder against any person listed in subdivision (a)

218.title: Derailing a train
218.plain: Unlawfully obstructing or setting fire to railroad track or bridges with intent to derail or wreck a train is a felony punishable by life in state prison without possibility of parole.
acts: throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad
places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle

218.1.title: Obstructing railroad track with gross negligence
218.1.plain: Unlawfully and with gross negligence placing an obstruction on a railroad track that damages or derails a train or injures a passenger or employee is punishable in county jail, under Section 1170(h), or by fine.
acts: places or causes to be placed any obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad

219.title: Wrecking a train
219.plain: Unlawfully obstructing, blowing up, or burning railroad track or bridges with intent to wreck a train and doing so is a felony; death or life without parole if someone dies, otherwise life with parole.
acts: throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad
places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle

219.1.title: Wrecking a common carrier vehicle
219.1.plain: Throwing a missile at, or doing an unlawful act to, a common carrier vehicle to wreck it and cause bodily harm, and doing so, is a felony punishable under Section 1170(h) for two, four, or six years.
acts: throws, hurls or projects at a vehicle operated by a common carrier

219.2.title: Throwing objects at trains, buses, or vessels
219.2.plain: Willfully throwing a hard object or shooting a missile at a train, bus, or passenger or freight vessel is punishable by county jail up to one year, state prison, or a fine up to $2,000.
acts: throws, hurls, or projects a stone or other hard substance, or shoots a missile, at a train, locomotive, railway car, caboose, cable railway car, street railway car, or bus or at a steam vessel or watercraft used for carrying passengers or freight on any of the waters within or bordering on this state

219.3.title: Dropping objects from a toll bridge
219.3.plain: Wilfully dropping or throwing any object or missile from a toll bridge is a misdemeanor.
acts: drops or throws any object or missile from any toll bridge

220.title: Assault with intent to commit a sex crime or mayhem
220.plain: Assault with intent to commit mayhem, rape, sodomy, or oral copulation carries two to six years in state prison, more if the victim is under 18, and life with parole during a first-degree burglary.
acts: assaults another with intent to commit mayhem, rape, sodomy, oral copulation, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, or 289
assaults another person under 18 years of age with the intent to commit rape, sodomy, oral copulation, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, or 289
assaults another with intent to commit rape, sodomy, oral copulation, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, or 289

222.title: Administering drugs to commit a felony
222.plain: Administering chloroform, ether, laudanum, a controlled substance, or another anaesthetic or intoxicating agent to help commit a felony is a felony punishable by 16 months, or two or three years.
acts: administering to another any chloroform, ether, laudanum, or any controlled substance, anaesthetic, or intoxicating agent

236.title: False imprisonment defined
236.plain: False imprisonment is the unlawful violation of the personal liberty of another; the section sets no punishment itself.
acts: the unlawful violation of the personal liberty of another

236.1.title: Human trafficking
236.1.plain: Depriving or violating another person's liberty to obtain forced labor or services, or to commit certain listed offenses, or inducing a minor into a commercial sex act, is human trafficking punishable by up to life in state prison.
acts: deprives or violates the personal liberty of another
causes, induces, or persuades, or attempts to cause, induce, or persuade, a person who is a minor at the time of commission of the offense to engage in a commercial sex act

236.2.title: Human trafficking victim indicators
236.2.plain: Requires law enforcement to use due diligence to identify human trafficking victims and to consider listed indicators of trafficking.

236.21.title: Victim interview rights
236.21.plain: Gives human trafficking victims the right to an advocate and support person at interviews and requires they be told of that right.

236.23.title: Human trafficking victim defense
236.23.plain: Creates an affirmative defense for a person coerced to commit an offense as a direct result of being a trafficking victim, and sets the relief if it succeeds.

236.24.title: Partner violence coercion defense
236.24.plain: Creates an affirmative defense for a person coerced to commit an offense as a direct result of intimate partner or sexual violence, and sets the relief if it succeeds.

236.3.title: Nuisance procedures after trafficking
236.3.plain: Applies public nuisance procedures and remedies to real property used to facilitate human trafficking after a conviction.

236.4.title: Human trafficking enhancements
236.4.plain: Great bodily injury during human trafficking adds a consecutive 5, 7, or 10 years in state prison, and a prior trafficking conviction adds a consecutive 5 years for each; the court may also add a fine up to $1,000,000.
acts: inflicts great bodily injury on a victim in the commission or attempted commission of a violation of Section 236.1
has previously been convicted of a violation of any crime specified in Section 236.1

236.5.title: Law enforcement endorsement letters
236.5.plain: Requires law enforcement to provide endorsement letters for human trafficking victims and sets rules for submitting and denying them.

236.6.title: Asset preservation proceedings
236.6.plain: Lets prosecutors petition for orders preserving assets of a person charged with human trafficking, and sets notice, claim, and hearing procedures.

236.7.title: Forfeiture for trafficking of minors
236.7.plain: Allows forfeiture of property used in or gained from human trafficking involving a commercial sex act with a minor, with limits for certain property.

236.8.title: Forfeiture petition procedure
236.8.plain: Sets the petition and notice procedure for forfeiture in trafficking cases involving a commercial sex act with a minor.

236.9.title: Forfeiture claims and hearing
236.9.plain: Sets how interested persons file claims and how the forfeiture hearing proceeds, including the burden of proof.

236.10.title: Orders to preserve forfeitable property
236.10.plain: Lets the court issue orders pending forfeiture to preserve property, including injunctions and receivers.

236.11.title: Forfeiture orders and liens
236.11.plain: Sets the court's orders on forfeited property and how lienholders are treated.

236.12.title: Distribution of forfeited property
236.12.plain: Sets how forfeited money and sale proceeds are distributed.

236.13.title: Victim Witness help for minors
236.13.plain: Requires that a minor trafficking victim be given Victim Witness Assistance Center help if the minor wishes.

236.14.title: Vacatur for trafficking victims
236.14.plain: Lets a trafficking victim petition to vacate convictions, arrests, and adjudications for nonviolent offenses committed as a victim, and sets the procedure.

236.15.title: Vacatur for partner violence victims
236.15.plain: Lets a victim of intimate partner or sexual violence petition to vacate convictions for nonviolent offenses committed as a victim, and sets the procedure.

237.title: False imprisonment punishment
237.plain: False imprisonment is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to one year in county jail, and by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170 if done by violence, menace, fraud, or deceit.
acts: False imprisonment
False imprisonment of an elder or dependent adult by use of violence, menace, fraud, or deceit

240.title: Assault defined
240.plain: An assault is an unlawful attempt, coupled with a present ability, to commit a violent injury on another person; the section sets no punishment itself.
acts: an unlawful attempt, coupled with a present ability, to commit a violent injury on the person of another

241.title: Assault punishment
241.plain: Assault is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to six months in county jail, with higher fines and up to one year in jail when committed against certain officers and workers.
acts: assault
an assault is committed against the person of a parking control officer engaged in the performance of their duties

an assault is committed against the person of a peace officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, process server, traffic officer, code enforcement officer, animal control officer, or search and rescue member engaged in the performance of their duties

241.1.title: Assault on custodial officer
241.1.plain: Assault on a custodial officer is punishable by up to one year in county jail or by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: an assault is committed against the person of a custodial officer as defined in Section 831 or 831.5

241.2.title: Assault on school or park property
241.2.plain: Assault on school or park property is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed on school or park property against any person

241.3.title: Assault on public transportation
241.3.plain: Assault on any person on the property of, or a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against any person on the property of, or on a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

241.4.title: Assault on school police officer
241.4.plain: Assault is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to six months in county jail; against a school district police officer it is punishable by up to one year in county jail or under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: An assault is punishable

the assault is committed against the person of a peace officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties as a member of a police department of a school district pursuant to Section 38000 of the Education Code

241.5.title: Assault on highway worker
241.5.plain: Assault on a highway worker engaged in their duties is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties

241.6.title: Assault on school employee
241.6.plain: Assault on a school employee engaged in their duties or in retaliation for their duties is punishable by up to one year in county jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or in retaliation for an act performed in the course of his or her duties

241.7.title: Assault on juror
241.7.plain: A party to a jury case who assaults a juror or alternate juror during or after the case is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, up to one year in county jail, or imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: commits an assault against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action

241.8.title: Assault on armed forces member
241.8.plain: Assault on a member of the United States Armed Forces because of the victim's service is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: commits an assault against a member of the United States Armed Forces

242.title: Battery defined
242.plain: Defines battery as any willful and unlawful use of force or violence upon the person of another; it sets no punishment itself.

243.title: Battery punishments
243.plain: Battery is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail; battery on certain officers, with injury, with serious bodily injury, or on partners is punished more, up to four years under Section 1170(h) sentencing.
acts: A battery is punishable
a battery is committed against the person of a peace officer
a battery is committed against a custodial officer
a battery is committed against any person and serious bodily injury is inflicted on the person
a battery is committed against a spouse

243.1.title: Battery on a custodial officer
243.1.plain: Battery on a custodial officer who is performing their duties, where the offender knows or should know it, is punished by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of a custodial officer

243.2.title: Battery on school, park, or hospital grounds
243.2.plain: Battery on school property, park property, or hospital grounds is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed on school property, park property, or the grounds of a public or private hospital, against any person

243.25.title: Battery on an elder or dependent adult
243.25.plain: Battery on an elder or dependent adult, knowing of that status, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of an elder or a dependent adult

243.3.title: Battery on transportation workers or passengers
243.3.plain: Battery on a public transportation operator, driver, passenger, agent, or employee is punishable by up to a $10,000 fine and a year in county jail, or state prison for 16 months to three years if injury results.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus

243.35.title: Battery on public transportation property
243.35.plain: Battery on any person on the property or in a motor vehicle of a public transportation provider is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against any person on the property of, or in a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

243.4.title: Sexual battery
243.4.plain: Sexual battery is touching an intimate part of another, or causing another to touch, for sexual purposes against their will in specified circumstances; felony sexual battery carries up to four years in state prison.
acts: touches an intimate part of another person while that person is unlawfully restrained by the accused or an accomplice
touches an intimate part of another person who is institutionalized for medical treatment and who is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated
touches an intimate part of another person for the purpose of sexual arousal, sexual gratification, or sexual abuse

causes another, against that person’s will while that person is unlawfully restrained either by the accused or an accomplice, or is institutionalized for medical treatment and is seriously disabled or medically incapacitated, to masturbate or touch an intimate part of either of those persons or a third person
touches an intimate part of another person, if the touching is against the will of the person touched

243.5.title: Arrest for school assault or battery
243.5.plain: Allows a peace officer to arrest without a warrant for an assault or battery on school property during school activities, and defines school.

243.6.title: Battery on a school employee
243.6.plain: Battery on a school employee, knowing of that status, is punishable by county jail up to one year or a $2,000 fine; with injury, it may be punished under Section 1170(h) for 16 months to three years.
acts: a battery is committed against a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties

243.65.title: Battery on a highway worker
243.65.plain: Battery on a highway worker who is performing their duties, where the offender knows or should know it, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against the person of a highway worker

243.7.title: Battery on a juror
243.7.plain: A party to a case who commits a battery on a juror or alternate juror is punishable by a fine up to $5,000, county jail up to one year, or state prison for 16 months to three years.
acts: commits a battery against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action

243.8.title: Battery on a sports official
243.8.plain: Battery on a sports official around an organized athletic contest, where the offender knows or should know the victim is performing duties, is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: a battery is committed against a sports official

243.83.title: Interference at professional sporting events
243.83.plain: It is an infraction, punishable by a fine up to $250, for a spectator at a professional sporting event to throw objects on the field or court or enter the field or court without permission.
acts: Throw any object on or across the court or field of play with the intent to interfere with play or distract a player
Enter upon the court or field of play without permission from an authorized person

243.85.title: Notice at professional sports facilities
243.85.plain: Requires owners of professional sports facilities to post notices with a text and phone number for reporting a violent act.

243.9.title: Gassing by a jail inmate
243.9.plain: A person confined in a local detention facility who gasses a peace officer or facility employee is guilty of aggravated battery, punishable in county jail or by two, three, or four years in state prison.
acts: commits a battery by gassing upon the person of any peace officer

243.10.title: Battery on a service member because of service
243.10.plain: Battery on a member of the United States Armed Forces because of their service is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: commits a battery against a member of the United States Armed Forces because of the victim’s service in the United States Armed Forces

243.15.title: Battery by a jail inmate on a non-inmate
243.15.plain: A person confined in a city or county jail, industrial farm, or road camp who commits a battery on a non-inmate is punishable under Section 1170(h) or in county jail up to one year.
acts: commits a battery upon the person of any individual who is not himself or herself a person confined or sentenced therein

244.title: Throwing acid or caustic substance
244.plain: Willfully and maliciously throwing acid, a flammable substance, or caustic chemical on another to injure the flesh or disfigure the body is punishable by two, three, or four years in state prison.
acts: places or throws, or causes to be placed or thrown, upon the person of another, any vitriol, corrosive acid, flammable substance, or caustic chemical of any nature

244.5.title: Assault with a stun gun
244.5.plain: Assault on another with a stun gun or less lethal weapon is punishable by county jail up to one year or under Section 1170(h); on a peace officer or firefighter the term is up to four years.
acts: commits an assault upon the person of another with a stun gun or less lethal weapon
commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a stun gun or less lethal weapon

245.title: Assault with a deadly weapon or force
245.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon, firearm, or force likely to produce great bodily injury is punishable by state prison, with terms up to 12 years for machineguns or assault weapons, or on peace officers and firefighters.
acts: commits an assault upon the person of another with a deadly weapon or instrument other than a firearm
commits an assault upon the person of another with a firearm
commits an assault upon the person of another with a machinegun
commits an assault upon the person of another by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury
commits an assault upon the person of another with a semiautomatic firearm
commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter
commits an assault upon the person of a peace officer or firefighter with a semiautomatic firearm
commits an assault with a machinegun

245.1.title: Emergency rescue personnel defined
245.1.plain: Defines emergency rescue personnel for use in Section 148.2.

245.2.title: Assault on transportation workers or passengers
245.2.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily injury on a public transit operator, driver, agent, or passenger is punishable by three, four, or five years in state prison.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means of force likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of an operator, driver, or passenger on a bus

245.3.title: Assault on a custodial officer
245.3.plain: Assault with a deadly weapon or force likely to produce great bodily injury on a custodial officer performing their duties is punishable by three, four, or five years in state prison.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a custodial officer

245.5.title: Assault on a school employee
245.5.plain: Assault on a school employee performing their duties with a deadly weapon, firearm, or stun gun is punishable by state prison, up to eight years with a firearm.
acts: commits an assault with a deadly weapon or instrument, other than a firearm, or by any means likely to produce great bodily injury upon the person of a school employee
commits an assault with a firearm upon the person of a school employee
commits an assault upon the person of a school employee with a stun gun or taser

245.6.title: Hazing
245.6.plain: Hazing likely to cause serious bodily injury is a misdemeanor with a fine of $100 to $5,000 or county jail up to one year; hazing causing death or serious bodily injury may be a felony under Section 1170(h).
acts: engage in hazing
engages in hazing that results in death or serious bodily injury

246.title: Shooting at an inhabited dwelling or vehicle
246.plain: Maliciously and willfully discharging a firearm at an inhabited dwelling, occupied building, vehicle, or aircraft is a felony punishable by three, five, or seven years in state prison.
acts: discharge a firearm at an inhabited dwelling house, occupied building, occupied motor vehicle, occupied aircraft, inhabited housecar

246.1.title: Sale of vehicles used in shootings
246.1.plain: Requires the court to order a vehicle used in specified violent firearm offenses sold, and sets the notice, sale, and proceeds procedure.

246.3.title: Grossly negligent discharge of a firearm
246.3.plain: Willfully discharging a firearm or BB device in a grossly negligent manner that could result in injury or death is punishable by county jail up to one year, or for a firearm also under Section 1170(h).
acts: discharges a firearm in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person
discharges a BB device in a grossly negligent manner which could result in injury or death to a person

247.title: Shooting at an unoccupied aircraft, vehicle, or building
247.plain: Willfully and maliciously shooting at an unoccupied aircraft is a felony; shooting at an unoccupied motor vehicle or uninhabited building is punishable in county jail up to one year or in state prison.
acts: discharges a firearm at an unoccupied aircraft
discharges a firearm at an unoccupied motor vehicle or an uninhabited building or dwelling house

247.5.title: Laser discharged at aircraft
247.5.plain: Willfully and maliciously discharging a laser at an occupied aircraft is a misdemeanor (county jail up to one year) or a felony (16 months, two years, or three years).
acts: discharges a laser at an aircraft, whether in motion or in flight, while occupied

248.title: Light shined at aircraft
248.plain: Willfully shining a bright light at an aircraft to interfere with its operation is punishable by a fine up to $1,000, county jail up to one year, or both.
acts: willfully shines a light or other bright device, of an intensity capable of impairing the operation of an aircraft, at an aircraft

450.title: Arson definitions
450.plain: Defines "structure," "forest land," "property," "inhabited," "maliciously," and "recklessly" for the arson chapter.

451.title: Arson
451.plain: Arson is willfully and maliciously setting fire to or burning any structure, forest land, or property, or helping to do so; it is a felony with up to nine years in state prison when it causes great bodily injury.
acts: sets fire to or burns or causes to be burned
aids, counsels, or procures the burning of, any structure, forest land, or property

451.1.title: Arson sentence enhancements
451.1.plain: A person convicted of felony arson under Section 451 gets an extra three, four, or five years if, for example, they have a prior arson conviction, injured firefighters, or burned multiple structures.
acts: convicted of a felony violation of Section 451

451.5.title: Aggravated arson
451.5.plain: Aggravated arson is a deliberate, premeditated arson meant to injure people or damage property, by a repeat arsonist or causing over $10.1 million in losses or damaging five or more homes; punishable by 10 years to life.
acts: sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned, or aids, counsels, or procures the burning of any residence, structure, forest land, or property

452.title: Unlawfully causing a fire
452.plain: Recklessly setting fire to or burning any structure, forest land, or property is unlawfully causing a fire; it is a misdemeanor for property and up to six years in state prison when it causes great bodily injury.
acts: set fire to, burn, or cause to be burned any structure, forest land, or property

452.1.title: Unlawful fire sentence enhancements
452.1.plain: A person convicted of felony unlawfully causing a fire under Section 452 gets an extra one, two, or three years for each listed circumstance, such as a prior arson conviction or injured firefighters.
acts: convicted of a felony violation of Section 452

453.title: Possessing incendiary materials or devices
453.plain: Possessing, making, or disposing of flammable material or an incendiary device with intent to use it to set fire to any structure, forest land, or property is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: possesses, manufactures, or disposes of any flammable, or combustible material or substance, or any incendiary device in an arrangement or preparation

454.title: Arson during a state of emergency
454.plain: Committing arson or unlawfully causing a fire in an area under a proclaimed state of insurrection or state of emergency is punishable by three, five, or seven years in state prison, or up to nine years for serious arson.
acts: violates Section 451 or 452 during and within an area of any of the following

455.title: Attempted arson
455.plain: Willfully and maliciously attempting to set fire to or burn any structure, forest land, or property, or doing any preliminary act, is punishable by 16 months, two, or three years in state prison.
acts: attempts to set fire to or attempts to burn or to aid, counsel or procure the burning of any structure, forest land or property
commits any act preliminary thereto, or in furtherance thereof

456.title: Fines for arson
456.plain: Lets the court add a fine of up to $50,000 for a felony arson-chapter conviction, or twice the gross gain when the crime was committed for pecuniary gain.

457.title: Psychiatric exam for arson
457.plain: Lets the court order a person convicted under the arson chapter to undergo a psychiatric or psychological examination for sentencing.

457.1.title: Arson offender registration
457.1.plain: Requires people convicted of arson or attempted arson to register with local police; failing to register is a misdemeanor, and a willful violation by a convicted arsonist means 90 days to one year in county jail.
acts: violates any of the provisions thereof
willfully violates any of the provisions thereof

458.title: Cargo container defined
458.plain: Defines "cargo container" for the burglary chapter as a permanent, reusable receptacle of 1,000 cubic feet or more designed for carrying goods by vessel and other transport.

459.title: Burglary defined
459.plain: Burglary is entering a house, building, locked vehicle, or other listed place with intent to commit grand or petit larceny or any felony; the punishment is set in Section 461.
acts: enters any house, room, apartment, tenement, shop, warehouse, store, mill, barn, stable, outhouse or other building

459.5.title: Shoplifting
459.5.plain: Shoplifting is entering an open store with intent to steal property worth $950 or less; it is a misdemeanor, but people with certain serious prior convictions may be sentenced as felons.
acts: entering a commercial establishment

460.title: Degrees of burglary
460.plain: Makes burglary of an inhabited dwelling house, inhabited vessel, floating home, trailer coach, or inhabited part of a building first degree burglary, and all other burglary second degree.

461.title: Punishment for burglary
461.plain: First degree burglary is punished by two, four, or six years in state prison; second degree burglary by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: Burglary in the first degree
Burglary in the second degree

462.title: No probation for residential burglary
462.plain: Bars probation, except in unusual cases with reasons stated on the record, for anyone convicted of burglary of an inhabited dwelling, trailer coach, floating home, or inhabited part of a building.

462.5.title: Custodial institution burglary
462.5.plain: Burglary on jail or prison grounds to steal items for weapons, escape tools, or drugs bars probation if a felony, and as a misdemeanor means 90 days to one year in county jail, served consecutively.
acts: convicted of a felony custodial institution burglary
convicted of a misdemeanor custodial institution burglary

463.title: Looting
463.plain: Burglary, grand or petty theft, and certain trespass or vehicle theft committed during a declared emergency, under an evacuation order, or in an evacuation zone is looting, punishable by up to seven years in state prison.
acts: A violation of Section 459
A violation of Section 487 or subdivision (a) of Section 487a
Grand theft of a firearm
A violation of Section 488
A violation of Section 602
theft from an unlocked vehicle

463.2.title: Looting while impersonating emergency personnel
463.2.plain: Lets the court treat impersonating emergency personnel while committing looting as a factor in aggravation at sentencing, and defines "emergency personnel" and "impersonating."

464.title: Burglary with torch or explosives
464.plain: Entering any building with intent to commit a crime and opening or trying to open a vault or safe with a torch, burning device, or explosive is a felony punishable by three, five, or seven years.
acts: enters, either by day or by night, any building, whether inhabited or not, and opens or attempts to open any vault, safe, or other secure place

465.title: Unlawful entry of a vehicle
465.plain: Forcibly entering a vehicle, such as with a lock tool or by breaking a window, intending to commit theft or a felony is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: forcibly enters a vehicle

466.title: Possession of burglary tools
466.plain: Possessing lock picks, slim jims, signal extenders, or other tools intending to break into a building or vehicle, or making keys or instruments for that or for crime, is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a picklock, crow, keybit, crowbar, screwdriver, vise grip pliers, water-pump pliers, slidehammer, slim jim, tension bar, lock pick gun, tubular lock pick, bump key, floor-safe door puller, master key, ceramic or porcelain spark plug chips or pieces, key programming device or key duplicating device, signal extender, or other instrument or tool
makes or alters, or attempts to make or alter, a key or other instrument named above
makes, alters, or repairs any instrument or thing

466.1.title: Lock pick sales records
466.1.plain: A person who sells or provides lock picks or similar tools must record the buyer's identity on a bill of sale kept for one year and open to police; violating this is a misdemeanor.
acts: sells or provides a lock pick, a tension bar, a lock pick gun, a tubular lock pick, or a floor-safe door puller, to another
violates any provision of this section

466.3.title: Coin machine burglary tools
466.3.plain: Possessing a key, tool, explosive, or device (or a drawing or mold of one) designed to break into coin-operated machines, intending to steal from them, is punishable by up to one year in county jail, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: possesses a key, tool, instrument, explosive, or device, or a drawing, print, or mold of a key, tool, instrument, explosive, or device

466.5.title: Motor vehicle master keys
466.5.plain: Possessing or using a motor vehicle master key or wheel lock master key to commit an unlawful act, or knowingly making or selling such keys except to lawful users, is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a motor vehicle master key or a motor vehicle wheel lock master key
uses a motor vehicle master key to open a lock or operate the ignition switch of any motor vehicle
uses a motor vehicle wheel lock master key to open a wheel lock on any motor vehicle
manufactures for sale, advertises for sale, offers for sale, or sells a motor vehicle master key or a motor vehicle wheel lock master key

466.6.title: Ignition key making records
466.6.plain: A person who makes a vehicle ignition key for someone else other than by duplicating an existing key must record the customer's and vehicle's details on a work order kept for two years; violating this is a misdemeanor.
acts: makes a key capable of operating the ignition of a motor vehicle or personal property registered under the Vehicle Code for another
violates any provision of this subdivision

466.65.title: Motorcycle theft tools
466.65.plain: Possessing, giving, or lending a device to bypass a motorcycle's ignition, a motorcycle ignition, or tools such as boltcutters, intending to take or drive a motorcycle without the owner's consent, is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses, gives, or lends any device designed to bypass the factory-installed ignition of a motorcycle
possesses, gives, or lends any motorcycle ignition, or part thereof
possesses, gives, or lends any item of hardware

466.7.title: Unauthorized motor vehicle key
466.7.plain: Possessing a vehicle key known to have been made without the owner's or lawful possessor's consent, intending to use it for an unlawful act, is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a motor vehicle key

466.8.title: Locksmith work order records
466.8.plain: A person who makes a key to a home or business for someone else by onsite inspection must record the buyer's name, address, ID and other details on a work order and keep it two years; violating this is a misdemeanor.
acts: makes a key capable of opening any door or other means of entrance to any residence or commercial establishment for another
violates any provision of this subdivision

466.9.title: Code grabbing devices
466.9.plain: Possessing a code grabbing device, or using one to disarm a vehicle security alarm, with intent to use it in an unlawful act is a misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a code grabbing device
uses a code grabbing device to disarm the security alarm system of a motor vehicle

468.title: Sniperscopes
468.plain: Knowingly buying, selling, receiving, disposing of, concealing, or possessing a sniperscope (an infrared night-vision firearm attachment) is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail and a $1,000 fine.
acts: buys, sells, receives, disposes of, conceals, or has in his possession a sniperscope

469.title: Unauthorized keys to public buildings
469.plain: Knowingly making, duplicating, using, or possessing a key to a state, county, city, or public school building or area without authorization is a misdemeanor.
acts: makes, duplicates, causes to be duplicated, or uses, or attempts to make, duplicate, cause to be duplicated, or use, or has in his possession any key to a building or other area owned, operated, or controlled by the State of California, any state agency, board, or commission, a county, city, or any public school or community college district

470.title: Forgery defined
470.plain: Forgery is signing another's name, forging a seal or handwriting, falsifying official records, or making or passing false checks, bonds, deeds, and other listed documents, with intent to defraud; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: signs the name of another person or of a fictitious person to any of the items listed in subdivision (d)
counterfeits or forges the seal or handwriting of another
alters, corrupts, or falsifies any record of any will, codicil, conveyance, or other instrument
falsely makes, alters, forges, or counterfeits, utters, publishes, passes or attempts or offers to pass, as true and genuine, any of the following items
falsifies the acknowledgment of any notary public
issues an acknowledgment

470a.title: Forging a driver's license or ID card
470a.plain: Altering, forging, copying, or counterfeiting a government-issued driver's license or ID card to help commit forgery is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: alters, falsifies, forges, duplicates or in any manner reproduces or counterfeits any driver’s license or identification card issued by a governmental agency

470b.title: Possessing a forged driver's license or ID
470b.plain: Displaying or possessing a driver's license or ID card of the kind in Section 470a, intending it to be used to commit forgery, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: displays or causes or permits to be displayed or has in his or her possession any driver’s license or identification card of the type enumerated in Section 470a

471.title: Forging record entries
471.plain: Making, forging, or altering an entry in a book of records, or a record or return named in Section 470, with intent to defraud is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: makes, forges, or alters any entry in any book of records, or any instrument purporting to be any record or return specified in Section 470

471.5.title: Falsifying medical records
471.5.plain: Altering or modifying a person's medical record, or creating a false medical record, with fraudulent intent is a misdemeanor.
acts: alters or modifies the medical record of any person
creates any false medical record

472.title: Forging public or corporate seals
472.plain: Forging or counterfeiting a state, court, public officer's, or corporate seal or its impression, or possessing and concealing a known counterfeit seal, with intent to defraud is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: forges, or counterfeits the seal of this State
falsely makes, forges, or counterfeits any impression purporting to be an impression of any such seal
has in his possession any such counterfeited seal or impression thereof

473.title: Punishment for forgery
473.plain: Forgery is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; forgery of a check or similar item worth $950 or less is limited to one year in county jail unless the person has certain prior convictions.
acts: Forgery
guilty of forgery relating to a check, bond, bank bill, note, cashier’s check, traveler’s check, or money order

474.title: False telegraph or telephone messages
474.plain: Sending, delivering, or furnishing a false or forged message purporting to come from a telegraph or telephone office or another person, to deceive, injure, or defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $10,000 fine.
acts: sends by telegraph or telephone to any person a false or forged message
delivers or causes to be delivered to any person any such message
furnishes, or conspires to furnish, or causes to be furnished to any agent, operator, or employee

475.title: Possessing forged or blank checks
475.plain: Possessing or receiving forged items, or possessing blank or completed checks, money orders, and similar items, intending to complete, pass, or utter them to defraud, is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: possesses or receives
possesses any blank or unfinished check, note, bank bill, money order, or traveler’s check, whether real or fictitious
possesses any completed check, money order, traveler’s check, warrant or county order, whether real or fictitious

476.title: Fictitious or altered checks
476.plain: Making, passing, or possessing a fictitious or altered bill, note, or check of a real or fictitious financial institution, with intent to defraud, is forgery; the punishment is set in Section 473.
acts: makes, passes, utters, or publishes
attempts to pass, utter, or publish
has in his or her possession

476a.title: Bad checks (insufficient funds)
476a.plain: Writing or delivering a check knowing there are not enough funds or credit to cover it, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; $950 or less is generally county jail only.
acts: makes or draws or utters or delivers a check, draft, or order upon a bank or depositary, a person, a firm, or a corporation, for the payment of money

477.title: Counterfeiting coin or bullion
477.plain: Counterfeiting gold or silver coin, gold dust, or bullion, or knowingly selling or passing such counterfeits, with intent to defraud, is counterfeiting; the punishment is set in Section 478.
acts: counterfeits any of the species of gold or silver coin current in this State, or any kind or species of gold dust, gold or silver bullion, or bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets
sells, passes, or gives in payment such counterfeit coin, dust, bullion, bars, lumps, pieces, or nuggets
permits, causes, or procures the same to be sold, uttered, or passed

478.title: Punishment for counterfeiting
478.plain: Counterfeiting is punishable by two, three, or four years of imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: Counterfeiting

479.title: Possessing counterfeit coin or bullion
479.plain: Possessing or receiving counterfeit gold or silver coin, gold dust, or bullion intending to pass it, knowing it is counterfeit and intending to defraud, is punishable by two, three, or four years under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: has in his possession, or receives for any other person, any counterfeit gold or silver coin of the species current in this state
permits, causes or procures the same to be sold, uttered or passed

480.title: Counterfeiting equipment
480.plain: Making or knowingly possessing dies, plates, machines, or other things used to counterfeit coin, bullion, or bank notes is punishable by two, three, or four years under subdivision (h) of Section 1170, and the equipment must be destroyed.
acts: makes
has in his or her possession any die, plate, or any apparatus, paper, metal, machine, or other thing whatever

481.title: Forging railroad or steamship tickets
481.plain: Counterfeiting, forging, or altering a railroad or steamship ticket or pass, or circulating one with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $1,000 fine.
acts: counterfeits, forges, or alters any ticket, check, order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass
utters, publishes, or puts into circulation, any such counterfeit or altered ticket, check, or order, coupon, receipt for fare, or pass

481.1.title: Counterfeit transit fare media
481.1.plain: Counterfeiting, forging, or altering public transit fare media is punishable by up to one year in county jail or state prison; knowingly possessing it, or passing fare media to defraud, is up to one year in county jail.
acts: counterfeits, forges, or alters any fare media designed to entitle the holder to a ride on vehicles of a public transportation system
possesses any counterfeit, forged, or altered fare media
utters, publishes, or puts into circulation any fare media

482.title: Restoring canceled tickets
482.plain: Removing cancellation marks from a used railroad or steamship ticket or pass to reuse, sell, or defraud, or knowingly offering such a restored ticket, is punishable by up to six months in county jail and a $1,000 fine.
acts: removes, conceals, fills up, or obliterates, the cuts, marks, punch-holes, or other evidence of cancellation
offers for sale, or in payment of fare on the railroad or vessel of the company, such ticket, check, order, coupon, or pass

483.title: Selling nontransferable transit tickets
483.plain: Selling a ticket, pass, or other instrument for passage on a common carrier for use by someone not entitled to use it under its terms is a misdemeanor.
acts: sell to another any ticket, pass, scrip, mileage or commutation book, coupon, or other instrument for passage on a common carrier

483.5.title: Deceptive identification documents
483.5.plain: Making or selling fake-looking ID documents without a "NOT A GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT" mark, knowing they will be used to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony; possessing document-making devices is a misdemeanor.
acts: violates the provisions of subdivision (a)
violates the provisions of subdivision (b)

484.title: Theft defined
484.plain: Defines theft (stealing, embezzling, or obtaining property by false pretenses), sets how the value of property and services is measured, and creates presumptions of intent for unreturned leased or rented property.

484.1.title: False information to pawnbrokers
484.1.plain: Knowingly giving false information about your identity, ownership, or authority to sell property to get money from a pawnbroker or secondhand dealer, and receiving it, is theft; the court may also order restitution.
acts: gives false information or provides false verification as to the person’s true identity or as to the person’s ownership interest in property or the person’s authority to sell property
receives money or other valuable consideration from the pawnbroker or secondhand dealer

484b.title: Diverting construction funds
484b.plain: Receiving money for construction services, labor, or materials and willfully diverting it to another use is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony, and a $10,000 fine, if over $2,350; otherwise a misdemeanor.
acts: receives money for the purpose of obtaining or paying for services, labor, materials or equipment
fails to apply such money for such purpose
diverts the funds to a use other than that for which the funds were received

484c.title: False vouchers for construction loans
484c.plain: Submitting a false voucher to get construction loan funds and not using the funds for the stated purpose is embezzlement.
acts: submits a false voucher to obtain construction loan funds

484d.title: Access card definitions
484d.plain: Defines "cardholder," "access card," "card issuer," "retailer," "counterfeit access card," "traffic," "card making equipment," and related terms for the access card crimes in Sections 484e to 484j.

484e.title: Access card theft
484e.plain: Selling or transferring someone's access card without consent, acquiring cards in four or more names in a year, or taking card account information to use fraudulently is grand theft; holding a card to misuse it is petty theft.
acts: sells, transfers, or conveys, an access card
acquires access cards issued in the names of four or more persons
acquires or retains possession of an access card
acquires or retains possession of access card account information with respect to an access card validly issued to another person

484f.title: Counterfeit access cards and forged card slips
484f.plain: Making or using a counterfeit access card, or signing another's or a fictitious name to an access card or card sales slip, with intent to defraud is forgery.
acts: designs, makes, alters, or embosses a counterfeit access card
utters or otherwise attempts to use a counterfeit access card
signs the name of another or of a fictitious person to an access card, sales slip, sales draft, or instrument for the payment of money which evidences an access card transaction

484g.title: Fraudulent use of access cards
484g.plain: Using a stolen, altered, forged, expired, or revoked access card, or falsely claiming to hold a card never issued, to get money or goods with intent to defraud is theft; over $950 in six months is grand theft.
acts: uses, for the purpose of obtaining money, goods, services, or anything else of value, an access card or access card account information that has been altered, obtained, or retained in violation of Section 484e or 484f
obtains money, goods, services, or anything else of value by representing

484h.title: Retailer access card fraud
484h.plain: A retailer or other person who, with intent to defraud, accepts a stolen, counterfeit, forged, expired, or revoked access card and takes payment, or bills for card sales not furnished, commits theft; over $950 in six months is grand theft.
acts: Furnishes money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of an access card
Presents for payment a sales slip or other evidence of an access card transaction, and receives payment therefor

484i.title: Incomplete cards and card-making equipment
484i.plain: Possessing an incomplete access card to complete it without consent is a misdemeanor; altering card account information to defraud is forgery; making or trafficking card-making equipment to counterfeit cards is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: possesses an incomplete access card
makes, alters, varies, changes, or modifies access card account information on any part of an access card
authorizes or consents to alteration, variance, change, or modification of access card account information by another
designs, makes, possesses, or traffics in card making equipment or incomplete access cards

484j.title: Publishing access card numbers and codes
484j.plain: Publishing the number or code of an access card, PIN, password, access code, debit card or bank account number, intending it be used to avoid lawful charges or to defraud, is a misdemeanor.
acts: publishes the number or code of an existing, canceled, revoked, expired or nonexistent access card, personal identification number, computer password, access code, debit card number, bank account number, or the numbering or coding which is employed in the issuance of access cards

485.title: Keeping lost property
485.plain: A person who finds lost property while knowing or able to learn who owns it, and keeps it without first making reasonable efforts to find and return it to the owner, is guilty of theft.
acts: appropriates such property to his own use, or to the use of another person not entitled thereto

486.title: Degrees of theft
486.plain: Divides theft into two degrees: grand theft and petty theft.

487.title: Grand theft defined
487.plain: Lists the cases that are grand theft, such as property worth more than $950, farm crops or aquacultural products over $250, employee theft of $950 or more in 12 months, theft from the person, and theft of an automobile or firearm, and allows aggregating related thefts.

487a.title: Theft of livestock and carcasses
487a.plain: Stealing, fraudulently taking, or obtaining by fraud horses, cattle, goats, sheep, pigs, and similar animals, or stealing their carcasses or parts of carcasses, is grand theft.
acts: steals, takes, carries, leads, or drives away any horse, mare, gelding, any bovine animal, any caprine animal, mule, jack, jenny, sheep, lamb, hog, sow, boar, gilt, barrow, or pig
appropriates that same property
defrauds any other person of that same property
causes or procures others to report falsely of his or her wealth or mercantile character
steal, take, transport or carry the carcass of any bovine, caprine, equine, ovine, or suine animal or of any mule, jack or jenny
appropriate such property
steal, take, transport, or carry any portion of the carcass of any bovine, caprine, equine, ovine, or suine animal or of any mule, jack, or jenny

487b.title: Severing real estate worth $250 or more
487b.plain: Stealing property worth $250 or more by severing it from someone else's real estate is grand theft, punishable by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: converts real estate of the value of two hundred fifty dollars ($250) or more into personal property by severance from the realty of another

487c.title: Severing real estate worth under $250
487c.plain: Stealing property worth less than $250 by severing it from someone else's real estate is petty theft, punishable by up to one year in county jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both.
acts: converts real estate of the value of less than two hundred fifty dollars ($250) into personal property by severance from the realty of another

487d.title: Theft of gold dust from mining claims
487d.plain: Stealing or trying to steal another's gold dust, amalgam, or quicksilver from a mining claim, tunnel, sluice, or similar works is grand theft, punishable by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: steals, takes, and carries away, or attempts to take, steal, and carry from any mining claim, tunnel, sluice, undercurrent, riffle box, or sulfurate machine, another’s gold dust, amalgam, or quicksilver

487e.title: Theft of a companion animal over $950
487e.plain: Stealing another person's pet or other companion animal worth more than $950 is grand theft.
acts: steals, takes, or carries away a companion animal of another

487f.title: Theft of a companion animal up to $950
487f.plain: Stealing another person's pet or other companion animal worth $950 or less is petty theft.
acts: steals, takes, or carries away a companion animal of another

487g.title: Theft of animals for commercial use
487g.plain: Stealing another's animal, or getting it by fraud, for sale, medical research, slaughter, or other commercial use is punishable by up to one year in county jail or by state prison.
acts: takes or carries away any animal of another
defrauds another person of any animal

487h.title: Cargo theft
487h.plain: Stealing another's cargo (goods loaded in a trailer, railcar, or cargo container, awaiting or in transit) worth more than $950 is grand theft.
acts: steals, takes, or carries away cargo of another

487i.title: Defrauding public housing programs
487i.plain: Defrauding a public housing authority's housing program of more than $400 is grand theft.
acts: defrauds a housing program of a public housing authority

487j.title: Theft of copper materials
487j.plain: Stealing another's copper wire, cable, tubing, piping, or other copper materials worth more than $950 is grand theft, punishable by up to one year in county jail and a $2,500 fine, or as a felony with a $10,000 fine.
acts: steals, takes, or carries away copper materials of another

487k.title: Theft of agricultural equipment
487k.plain: Stealing tractors, all-terrain vehicles, or other agricultural equipment used to produce food for the public, worth more than $950, is grand theft.
acts: steals, takes, or carries away tractors, all-terrain vehicles, or other agricultural equipment, or any portion thereof

487m.title: Wage theft by an employer
487m.plain: An employer's intentional theft of more than $950 in wages from one employee, or more than $2,350 from two or more employees, within 12 months may be punished as grand theft; wages may be recovered as restitution.
acts: theft of wages

488.title: Petty theft defined
488.plain: Provides that theft that is not grand theft is petty theft.

489.title: Punishment for grand theft
489.plain: Grand theft of a firearm is punishable by 16 months, two, or three years in state prison; other grand theft, including livestock theft, by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: Grand theft
the theft of a firearm
a violation of Section 487a

490.title: Punishment for petty theft
490.plain: Petty theft is punishable by a fine up to $1,000, up to six months in county jail, or both.
acts: Petty theft

490a.title: Larceny read as theft
490a.plain: Provides that any California law referring to larceny, embezzlement, or stealing is to be read as if the word "theft" were used instead.

490.1.title: Petty theft of $50 or less as infraction
490.1.plain: Petty theft of $50 or less may be charged as a misdemeanor or, if the person has no other theft conviction, as an infraction punishable by a fine up to $250.
acts: Petty theft

490.2.title: Petty theft of $950 or less
490.2.plain: Obtaining property by theft worth $950 or less is petty theft punished as a misdemeanor, but may be punished under subdivision (h) of Section 1170 if the person has certain serious or sex-offense prior convictions.
acts: obtaining any property by theft

490.3.title: Aggregating theft values
490.3.plain: Allows the value of property stolen in one or more acts of theft or shoplifting to be added together in a single count to decide the degree of theft.

490.4.title: Organized retail theft
490.4.plain: Acting with others to steal merchandise from stores or online marketplaces for resale, receiving such stolen goods, stealing as part of an organized plan, or directing such theft is organized retail theft, punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: Acts in concert with one or more persons to steal merchandise from one or more merchant’s premises or online marketplace
Acts in concert with two or more persons to receive, purchase, or possess merchandise described in paragraph (1)
Acts as an agent of another individual or group of individuals to steal merchandise from one or more merchant’s premises or online marketplaces
Recruits, coordinates, organizes, supervises, directs, manages, or finances another to undertake any of the acts described in paragraph (1) or (2) or any other statute defining theft of merchandise

490.5.title: Shoplifting and library theft
490.5.plain: A first conviction for petty theft of store merchandise or library materials carries a mandatory $50 to $1,000 fine and up to six months in county jail; the section also allows civil damages and lets merchants and libraries detain suspects.
acts: petty theft involving merchandise taken from a merchant’s premises or a book or other library materials taken from a library facility

490.6.title: Amusement park detentions
490.6.plain: Lets amusement park employees detain, for a reasonable time, a person they have probable cause to believe is violating lawful park rules, treats refusing to comply or leave as obstructing business under Section 602.1, and gives a defense in civil suits.

490.7.title: Taking free newspapers
490.7.plain: Taking more than 25 copies of the current issue of a free newspaper to recycle, sell, deprive others of it, or harm a competitor is an infraction; repeat violations can be a misdemeanor with up to 10 days in county jail.
acts: take more than twenty-five (25) copies of the current issue of a free or complimentary newspaper

490.8.title: Retail crime restraining orders
490.8.plain: Courts may bar people convicted of, or repeatedly arrested for, shoplifting, retail theft, vandalism, or assault at a store from entering it for up to two years; violating such an order is a misdemeanor.
acts: violation of an order issued pursuant to this section

491.title: Companion animals as property
491.plain: Treats companion animals as personal property valued like other property and defines "companion animal" for this section, excluding feral animals.

492.title: Value of stolen debt instruments
492.plain: Sets how to value a stolen evidence of debt or other written instrument, based on the amount due or secured or the value of the property it shows title to.

493.title: Value of stolen passage tickets
493.plain: Sets the value of a stolen railroad, vessel, or other public conveyance ticket as the price usually charged for a like passage.

494.title: Unissued instruments covered by larceny
494.plain: Applies the larceny chapter to completed instruments for payment of money, evidence of debt, public securities, or passage tickets even if never issued or delivered.

495.title: Severed fixtures covered by larceny
495.plain: Applies the larceny chapter to fixtures or parts of real property severed at the time of the taking, as if severed earlier by another person.

496.title: Receiving stolen property
496.plain: Buying, receiving, concealing, selling, or withholding property knowing it was stolen or obtained by theft or extortion, or a dealer buying it without reasonable inquiry, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: buys or receives any property that has been stolen or that has been obtained in any manner constituting theft or extortion
conceals, sells, withholds, or aids in concealing, selling, or withholding any property from the owner
buys or receives any property

496.5.title: Automotive property theft for resale
496.5.plain: Possessing over $950 of property taken through vehicle theft, break-ins, or tampering, not for personal use but intending to sell or exchange it, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: possesses property that was acquired through one or more acts of theft from a vehicle, unlawful entry of a vehicle, burglary of a locked vehicle, or vehicle tampering as defined in Section 10852 of the Vehicle Code

496.6.title: Unlawful deprivation of a retail business opportunity
496.6.plain: Possessing over $950 of property taken by shoplifting, theft, or burglary from a retail business, not for personal use but intending to sell, exchange, or return it, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: possesses property unlawfully that was acquired through one or more acts of shoplifting, theft, or burglary from a retail business

496a.title: Junk dealers receiving utility metals
496a.plain: A junk, metal, or secondhand dealer who buys wire, cable, copper, or similar metals ordinarily belonging to a railroad or utility without due diligence about the seller's right is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: buys or receives any wire, cable, copper, lead, solder, mercury, iron, or brass

496b.title: Dealers receiving library materials
496b.plain: A secondhand book dealer who buys library-marked books or materials without diligent inquiry commits criminally receiving property: up to one year in county jail if worth over $50, up to one month if $50 or under.
acts: buys or receives any book, manuscript, map, chart, or other work of literature, belonging to, and bearing any mark or indicia of ownership by a public or incorporated library, college or university

496c.title: Copying private title records
496c.plain: Copying private title-company records without the owner's consent to use them in the title business, inducing someone to do so, or knowingly receiving such copies is theft.
acts: copy, transcribe, photograph or otherwise make a record or memorandum of the contents of any private and unpublished paper, book, record, map or file
induce another to violate the provisions of this section
receive or acquire from another any copy, transcription, photograph or other record or memorandum of the contents of any private and unpublished paper, book, record, map or file

496d.title: Receiving stolen vehicles and vessels
496d.plain: Buying, receiving, concealing, selling, or withholding a motor vehicle, trailer, special construction equipment, or vessel knowing it was stolen is punishable by up to three years under county felony sentencing or up to one year in county jail.
acts: buys or receives any motor vehicle, as defined in Section 415 of the Vehicle Code, any trailer, as defined in Section 630 of the Vehicle Code, any special construction equipment, as defined in Section 565 of the Vehicle Code, or any vessel
