conceals, sells, withholds, or aids in concealing, selling, or withholding any motor vehicle, trailer, special construction equipment, or vessel from the owner

496e.title: Scrap dealers possessing stolen public fixtures
496e.plain: A scrap metal dealer who possesses stolen fire hydrants, manhole covers, street lights, and similar public or utility items knowing they were stolen, or fails to report possessing them, faces an added fine up to $5,000.
acts: possesses any of the following items
fails to report possession of the items

497.title: Bringing stolen property into the state
497.plain: A person who steals or embezzles property in another state or country, or receives it knowing it was stolen, and brings it into California may be punished as if the crime happened in California.
acts: steals or embezzles the property of another
receives such property
brings the same into this state

498.title: Theft of utility services
498.plain: Diverting utility services, tampering with meters or utility property, making unauthorized connections, or knowingly using diverted service to avoid paying is a misdemeanor; over $950 or a prior conviction allows county jail or state prison.
acts: Diverts or causes to be diverted utility services, by any means
Prevents any utility meter, or other device used in determining the charge for utility services, from accurately performing its measuring function
Tampers with any property owned by or used by the utility to provide utility services
Makes or causes to be made any connection with or reconnection with property owned or used by the utility to provide utility services
Uses or receives the direct benefit of all or a portion of utility services

499.title: Repeat temporary taking of vehicles or vessels
499.plain: A person convicted under Section 499b involving a vehicle or vessel after a prior qualifying vehicle theft conviction and jail term, or after two prior 499b convictions, faces up to one year in county jail or up to three years in state prison.
acts: convicted of a violation of Section 499b, involving a vehicle or vessel

499b.title: Joyriding on a bicycle or vessel
499b.plain: Taking someone's bicycle or vessel without permission to use it temporarily is a misdemeanor, punishable by up to three months in county jail for a bicycle or up to one year for a vessel.
acts: take any bicycle
take any vessel

499c.title: Theft of trade secrets
499c.plain: Stealing, misappropriating, or copying a trade secret to deprive its owner or use it is theft; bribing an employee to hand over a trade secret, or accepting such a bribe, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or as a felony.
acts: Steals, takes, carries away, or uses without authorization, a trade secret
Fraudulently appropriates any article representing a trade secret entrusted to him or her
makes or causes to be made a copy of any article representing a trade secret
promises, offers or gives, or conspires to promise or offer to give, to any present or former agent, employee or servant of another, a benefit
solicits, accepts, receives or takes a benefit

499d.title: Unauthorized taking of an aircraft
499d.plain: Operating or taking another's aircraft without consent, intending to deprive the owner of it permanently or temporarily, or being an accomplice, is a felony punishable by up to one year in county jail or under county felony sentencing, or a fine up to $10,000.
acts: operates or takes an aircraft not his own
is a party or accessory to or an accomplice in any operation or unauthorized taking or stealing

500.title: Failing to transmit money abroad
500.plain: A person who takes money to send to a foreign country and does not forward it, commit equivalent funds, or refund it within 10 days commits a crime punishable by up to three years if $950 or more.
acts: fails to do at least one of the following acts

501.title: Proof of stolen money in larceny trials
501.plain: Says that in a larceny or embezzlement trial the description of stolen money, bank notes, stock certificates, or securities is proved even if the exact kind or denomination is not proved.

502.title: Computer crimes
502.plain: Knowingly accessing, damaging, copying, or using computers, data, or computer services without permission, disrupting service, or introducing viruses is a crime; serious violations are punishable by up to three years under county felony sentencing.
acts: alters, damages, deletes, destroys, or otherwise uses any data, computer, computer system, or computer network
takes, copies, or makes use of any data from a computer, computer system, or computer network
takes or copies any supporting documentation
uses or causes to be used computer services
adds, alters, damages, deletes, or destroys any data, computer software, or computer programs which reside or exist internal or external to a computer, computer system, or computer network
disrupts or causes the disruption of computer services or denies or causes the denial of computer services to an authorized user of a computer, computer system, or computer network
provides or assists in providing a means of accessing a computer, computer system, or computer network
accesses or causes to be accessed any computer, computer system, or computer network
introduces any computer contaminant into any computer, computer system, or computer network
uses the internet domain name or profile of another individual, corporation, or entity in connection with the sending of one or more electronic mail messages or posts

disrupts or causes the disruption of government computer services or denies or causes the denial of government computer services to an authorized user of a government computer, computer system, or computer network

adds, alters, damages, deletes, or destroys any data, computer software, or computer programs which reside or exist internal or external to a public safety infrastructure computer system computer, computer system, or computer network

disrupts or causes the disruption of public safety infrastructure computer system computer services or denies or causes the denial of computer services to an authorized user of a public safety infrastructure computer system computer, computer system, or computer network
provides or assists in providing a means of accessing a computer, computer system, or public safety infrastructure computer system computer, computer system, or computer network
introduces any computer contaminant into any public safety infrastructure computer system computer, computer system, or computer network

502.01.title: Forfeiture of computers and telecom devices
502.01.plain: Sets the court procedure for forfeiting a convicted defendant's computers, software, or illegal telecommunications equipment, protecting other owners' interests and directing how the property or sale proceeds are distributed.

502.5.title: Removing improvements from mortgaged property
502.5.plain: Removing or disposing of a house, barn, pump, or other attached improvement from mortgaged or foreclosed real property, with intent to defraud the lender or buyer and without written consent, is larceny.
acts: takes, removes or carries away from such mortgaged or encumbered premises, or otherwise disposes of or permits the taking, removal or carrying away or otherwise disposing of any house, barn, windmill, water tank, pump, engine or other part of the freehold

502.6.title: Payment card skimmers and reencoders
502.6.plain: Knowingly possessing or using a card scanning device or reencoder with intent to defraud, to capture or place payment card data without the cardholder's permission, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail.
acts: possesses a scanning device
uses a scanning device to access, read, obtain, memorize or store, temporarily or permanently, information encoded on the magnetic strip or stripe of a payment card
possesses a reencoder
uses a reencoder to place encoded information on the magnetic strip or stripe of a payment card or any electronic medium that allows an authorized transaction to occur

502.7.title: Telephone service fraud
502.7.plain: Avoiding telephone or telegraph charges by fraud, making or selling devices or plans to avoid toll charges, publishing card numbers for that purpose, or selling use of one's calling card is a misdemeanor or felony.
acts: avoids or attempts to avoid, or aids, abets or causes another to avoid the lawful charge, in whole or in part, for telephone or telegraph service
Makes, possesses, sells, gives, or otherwise transfers to another, or offers or advertises any instrument, apparatus, or device
Sells, gives, or otherwise transfers to another or offers, or advertises plans or instructions for making or assembling an instrument, apparatus, or device
publishes the number or code of an existing, canceled, revoked, expired, or nonexistent credit card, or the numbering or coding which is employed in the issuance of credit cards
receives anything of value

502.8.title: Illegal telecommunications equipment
502.8.plain: Advertising, possessing, or using illegal telecommunications equipment to avoid charges is a misdemeanor; possessing it to sell can bring county jail or state prison, and repeat use or dealing in 10 or more items is a felony.
acts: advertises illegal telecommunications equipment
possesses or uses illegal telecommunications equipment
possesses illegal telecommunications equipment
possesses 10 or more items of illegal telecommunications equipment
manufactures 10 or more items of illegal telecommunications equipment

502.9.title: Elder victims as aggravating factor
502.9.plain: Makes an elder or dependent victim a circumstance in aggravation when a court sets the term for a felony under this chapter.

503.title: Embezzlement defined
503.plain: Defines embezzlement as the fraudulent appropriation of property by a person to whom it has been entrusted.

504.title: Embezzlement by public and corporate officers
504.plain: Public officers, their deputies and staff, and officers or agents of associations or corporations who fraudulently take or hide property they hold in trust are guilty of embezzlement; this section states no punishment.
acts: appropriates to any use or purpose not in the due and lawful execution of that person’s trust
secretes it

504a.title: Disposing of leased or unpaid-for property
504a.plain: Fraudulently removing, concealing, or disposing of leased property, or property held under an unfinished purchase contract, is embezzlement, as is doing so knowingly by a person in possession; no punishment is stated here.
acts: remove, conceal or dispose of any goods, chattels or effects
remove, conceal or dispose of the same

504b.title: Debtor keeping sale proceeds owed to secured party
504b.plain: A debtor who sells secured property, willfully and with intent to defraud fails to pay the secured party what is owed, and keeps the money is guilty of embezzlement, punished as provided in Section 514.
acts: fails to pay to the secured party the amounts due under the security agreement
appropriates the money to his or her own use

505.title: Embezzlement by carriers
505.plain: A carrier or other person holding property for transportation for hire who fraudulently appropriates it, whether or not the package was broken open, is guilty of embezzlement; no punishment is stated here.
acts: appropriates it to any use or purpose inconsistent with the safe keeping of such property and its transportation according to his trust

506.title: Embezzlement by trustees, agents, and contractors
506.plain: Trustees, agents, executors, collectors and others entrusted with property who fraudulently take or hide it, and contractors who divert money paid to them, are guilty of embezzlement; no punishment is stated here.
acts: appropriates it to any use or purpose not in the due and lawful execution of his trust
secretes it
appropriates money paid to him for any use or purpose, other than for that which he received it

506a.title: Debt collectors covered by Section 506
506a.plain: Treats collectors and others in the debt-collection business who violate Section 506 as agents under that section, to be prosecuted and punished under it, and defines "collector".

506b.title: Violating real property sales contract rules
506b.plain: Violating Civil Code Section 2985.3 or 2985.4 on real property sales contracts is a crime punishable by a fine up to $10,000, up to one year in county jail, or a felony jail term.
acts: violates Section 2985.3 or 2985.4 of the Civil Code

507.title: Embezzlement by bailees, tenants, and lodgers
507.plain: A person entrusted with property as a bailee, tenant, or lodger, or with a power of attorney to sell it, who fraudulently converts or hides it is guilty of embezzlement; no punishment is stated here.
acts: converts the same or the proceeds thereof to his own use
secretes it or them

508.title: Embezzlement by employees
508.plain: A clerk, agent, or servant who fraudulently takes or hides another's property that came into their care through their employment is guilty of embezzlement; no punishment is stated here.
acts: appropriates to his own use
secretes

509.title: No separate taking needed for embezzlement
509.plain: States that a distinct act of taking is not necessary to constitute embezzlement.

510.title: Debt instruments can be embezzled
510.plain: States that an executed evidence of debt negotiable by delivery only can be embezzled whether or not it was delivered or issued as a valid instrument.

511.title: Good-faith claim of title defense
511.plain: Makes it a defense to embezzlement that the property was taken openly under a good-faith claim of title, but not for keeping property to offset debts owed.

512.title: Intent to restore is no defense
512.plain: States that intending to restore embezzled property is no defense or mitigation unless it was restored before charges were filed.

513.title: Restoring property before charges
513.plain: Lets the court reduce punishment, but gives no defense, when the accused voluntarily restores or tenders embezzled property before charges are filed.

514.title: Punishment for embezzlement
514.plain: Embezzlement is punished like theft of property of the same value or kind; embezzling public funds is a felony punishable by state prison and bars the person from holding state office.
acts: guilty of embezzlement

515.title: Elder victims as aggravating factor
515.plain: Makes an elder or dependent victim a circumstance in aggravation when sentencing a felony embezzlement conviction.

518.title: Extortion defined
518.plain: Defines extortion as obtaining property, other consideration, or an official act through wrongful force or fear or under color of official right, defines "consideration," and excludes certain minors.

519.title: Threats that constitute extortion
519.plain: Lists the threats that can induce the fear needed for extortion, such as threats of injury, accusing someone of a crime, exposing secrets, or reporting immigration status.

520.title: Extortion by force or threat
520.plain: Extorting property or other consideration by force or a threat listed in Section 519, short of robbery or carjacking, is punishable by two, three, or four years under the felony jail sentencing rules.
acts: extorts property or other consideration from another

521.title: Extortion under color of official right
521.plain: Committing extortion under color of official right is a misdemeanor where no different punishment is prescribed; this section states no term.
acts: commits any extortion under color of official right

522.title: Obtaining a signature by extortion
522.plain: Using extortionate means to get someone's signature on a paper that would transfer property or create a debt is punished as if the debt or right itself were obtained; no term is stated here.
acts: obtains from another his signature to any paper or instrument

523.title: Threatening letters and ransomware
523.plain: Sending a threatening letter to extort property, or introducing ransomware to extort it, is punished as if the property had actually been obtained; ransomware is punished under Section 520.
acts: sends or delivers to any person any letter or other writing
introduces ransomware into any computer, computer system, or computer network

524.title: Attempted extortion
524.plain: Attempting to extort property or other consideration by a threat listed in Section 519 is punishable by up to one year in county jail or state prison, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
acts: attempts, by means of any threat, such as is specified in Section 519 of this code, to extort property or other consideration from another

525.title: Elder victims as aggravating factor
525.plain: Makes an elder or dependent victim a circumstance in aggravation when sentencing a felony extortion conviction.

526.title: Delivering fake court papers to obtain property
526.plain: Delivering a paper made to look like a court order or process, to get property or other consideration from someone, is a misdemeanor; each delivery is a separate offense.
acts: delivers or causes to be delivered to the other person any paper, document or written, typed or printed form

527.title: Selling or printing fake court forms
527.plain: Selling, printing, publishing, or distributing papers designed to look like court orders or process is a misdemeanor; each act is a separate offense, and the court may order the papers destroyed.
acts: sell or offer for sale, print, publish, or distribute any paper, document or written, typed or printed form

528.title: Marrying under a false identity
528.plain: Falsely impersonating another person and, in that assumed character, marrying or pretending to marry someone is a felony; this section states no term.
acts: falsely personates another, and in such assumed character marries or pretends to marry, or to sustain the marriage relation towards another

528.5.title: Online impersonation
528.5.plain: Knowingly and without consent credibly impersonating a real person online or electronically to harm, intimidate, threaten, or defraud someone is punishable by up to one year in county jail, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: credibly impersonates another actual person through or on an Internet Web site or by other electronic means

529.title: False personation
529.plain: Falsely impersonating another and, in that character, posting bail, signing or proving documents, or doing acts that could create liability or benefit is punishable by up to $10,000, county jail, or a felony jail term.
acts: falsely personates another in either his or her private or official capacity
Becomes bail or surety for any party in any proceeding whatever
Verifies, publishes, acknowledges, or proves, in the name of another person, any written instrument
Does any other act

529a.title: Fake birth or baptism certificates
529a.plain: Making or selling false birth or baptism certificates to deceive is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term; using or possessing one to pose as someone else carries up to one year.
acts: manufactures, produces, sells, offers, or transfers to another any document purporting to be either a certificate of birth or certificate of baptism
offers, displays, or has in his or her possession any false or counterfeit certificate of birth or certificate of baptism

529.5.title: Fake government ID documents
529.5.plain: Making or selling fake-looking government ID cards or driver's licenses, knowing they are not genuine, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail; knowingly possessing one carries a fine.
acts: manufactures, sells, offers for sale, or transfers any document, not amounting to counterfeit, purporting to be a government-issued identification card or driver’s license
possesses a document described in subdivision (a)

529.6.title: Impersonating a census taker
529.6.plain: Falsely posing as a census taker, or falsely taking on a census taker's activities, to interfere with the census or obtain information or consent to an unlawful search is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail.
acts: Falsely represents that they are a census taker
Falsely assumes some or all of the activities of a census taker

529.7.title: Obtaining DMV documents unlawfully
529.7.plain: Obtaining, or helping someone obtain, a driver's license, ID card, registration, or other DMV document, knowing that person is not entitled to it, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail.
acts: obtains, or assists another person in obtaining, a driver’s license, identification card, vehicle registration certificate, or any other official document issued by the Department of Motor Vehicles

530.title: Receiving property by false personation
530.plain: Falsely impersonating another and, in that character, receiving money or property meant for that person, intending to keep or divert it, is punished the same as larceny of that money or property.
acts: falsely personates another, in either his private or official capacity, and in such assumed character receives any money or property

530.5.title: Identity theft
530.5.plain: Obtaining and using someone's personal identifying information for an unlawful purpose, or acquiring, keeping, or selling it to defraud, is punishable by county jail up to one year or a felony jail term; mail theft is also covered.
acts: obtains personal identifying information
uses that information for any unlawful purpose
acquires or retains possession of the personal identifying information
sells, transfers, or conveys the personal identifying information
sells, transfers, or conveys that same personal identifying information
commits mail theft

530.55.title: Identity theft definitions
530.55.plain: Defines "person" and "personal identifying information" for the false personation and cheats chapter.

530.6.title: Identity theft victims' police reports and innocence
530.6.plain: Lets identity theft victims get a police report and investigation and petition a court for a determination of factual innocence, with sealing or labeling of records.

530.7.title: Identity theft victim database
530.7.plain: Requires the Department of Justice to keep a database and toll-free number of identity theft victims who submit a court order and fingerprints.

530.8.title: Victims' access to fraudulent account records
530.8.plain: Lets identity theft victims obtain records of applications or accounts opened in their name, with court enforcement and a civil action for noncompliance.

531.title: Fraudulent conveyances
531.plain: Being a party to a conveyance or other transaction made to defraud others or hinder creditors, or knowingly defending or transferring under it, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: is a party to any fraudulent conveyance of any lands, tenements, or hereditaments, goods or chattels
puts in, uses, avows, maintains, justifies, or defends the same
aliens, assigns, or sells any of the lands, tenements, hereditaments, goods, chattels, or other things before mentioned

531a.title: Fraudulent real property deeds
531a.plain: Executing, or filing, a deed to real property knowing the person signing has no interest in it, with intent to defraud, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year or a $5,000 fine, or both.
acts: executes or procures another to execute any instrument purporting to convey any real property
files or procures the filing of any such instrument

532.title: Obtaining property by false pretenses
532.plain: Defrauding someone of money, labor, or property by false representation, or getting credit by false reports of one's wealth, is punished the same as larceny of that money or property.
acts: defrauds any other person of money, labor, or property, whether real or personal
causes or procures others to report falsely of his or her wealth or mercantile character

532a.title: False financial statements to get credit
532a.plain: Making a false written statement about financial condition to obtain property, loans, or credit, or obtaining them on such a statement, is a misdemeanor; using a fictitious name or false identity can be a felony.
acts: make or cause to be made, either directly or indirectly or through any agency whatsoever, any false statement in writing
procures, upon the faith thereof
represents on a later day in writing that the statement theretofore made, if then again made on said day, would be then true

532b.title: California Stolen Valor Act
532b.plain: Fraudulently claiming to be a veteran or service member, or to have a military decoration, to get money, property, or benefits, or forging or using false military papers for that purpose, is a misdemeanor.
acts: fraudulently represents themselves as a veteran or ex-serviceman of a war in which the United States was engaged
fraudulently claims, or presents themselves, to be a veteran or member of the Armed Forces of the United States
fraudulently represents themselves to have been awarded a military decoration
forges documentation reflecting the awarding of a military decoration that the person has not received
misrepresents themselves as a member or veteran of the Armed Forces of the United States
utilizes falsified military identification
misrepresents themselves, as a member or veteran of the Armed Forces of the United States

532c.title: Giving away land with lottery or admission tickets
532c.plain: Offering or giving real property with winning drawing numbers or admission tickets and charging fees for its transfer is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: offers or gives with winning numbers at any drawing of numbers or with tickets of admission to places of public assemblage, any lot or parcel of real property

532d.title: False statements in charitable solicitations
532d.plain: Making a false factual statement about a charity, its costs, or the use of funds while soliciting or receiving donations, knowingly or negligently, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail or a $5,000 fine.
acts: makes, utters, or delivers, either orally or in writing, an unqualified statement of fact

532e.title: Construction fund kickbacks
532e.plain: A person who receives money to pay for construction work on real property and willfully rebates part of it to anyone contracting to provide that work is guilty of a misdemeanor.
acts: rebates any part of the money to or on behalf of anyone contracting with such person

532f.title: Mortgage fraud
532f.plain: Making or using misstatements in the mortgage lending process, taking proceeds from it, filing false documents, or (for brokers) steering borrowers into improper loans, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: makes any misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission during the mortgage lending process
uses or facilitates the use of any misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission
Receives any proceeds or any other funds in connection with a mortgage loan closing
Files or causes to be filed with the recorder of any county in connection with a mortgage loan transaction any document
causes a borrower to sign documents reflecting the terms of a business, commercial, or agricultural loan
causes a borrower to sign documents reflecting the terms of a bridge loan

533.title: Selling the same land twice
533.plain: After selling land or agreeing to sell it, willfully selling it again or agreeing to sell it to someone else to defraud purchasers is a felony punishable under the felony jail sentencing rules; no term is stated here.
acts: sells, barters, or disposes of the same tract of land or town lot
executes any bond or agreement to sell, barter, or dispose of the same land or lot

534.title: Selling real estate without spouse's consent
534.plain: A married person or registered domestic partner who falsely claims to be able to sell or mortgage real estate that needs the spouse's assent, and then conveys or mortgages it, is guilty of a felony; no term is stated here.
acts: conveys or mortgages the same

535.title: Mock auctions
535.plain: Obtaining money, property, or a signature through a false sale, auction, or mock auction is punishable by up to one year in county jail, a felony jail term, or a $2,000 fine, and a three-year ban on auctioneering.
acts: obtains any money or property from another, or obtains the signature of another to any written instrument

536.title: False accounts by commission merchants
536.plain: A commission merchant, broker, agent, factor, or consignee who willfully and corruptly gives the owner a false statement about the sale price, quality, quantity, or expenses of consigned property is guilty of a misdemeanor, up to six months in county jail.
acts: make, or cause to be made, to the principal or consignor of such commission merchant, agent, broker, factor, or consignee, a false statement

536a.title: Commission merchants' duty to report sales
536a.plain: Commission merchants, brokers, factors, and consignees must give the owner, on written demand, a true written statement of buyers, quantities, and prices for consigned property; violating this is a misdemeanor.
acts: to make, when accounting therefor or subsequently, upon the written demand of his principal or consignor, a true written statement

537.title: Defrauding innkeepers and restaurants
537.plain: Obtaining food, lodging, or services at a hotel, restaurant, campground, or similar place without paying, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to six months, or up to one year or state prison above $950; ski area fare-dodging is an infraction.
acts: obtains any food, fuel, services, or accommodations
obtains credit at an hotel, inn, restaurant, boardinghouse, lodginghouse, apartment house, bungalow court, motel, marina, marine facility, autocamp, or public or private campground
absconds
removes any part of his or her baggage therefrom
uses or attempts to use ski area facilities for which payment is required without paying as required
resells a ski lift ticket to another

537b.title: Defrauding livery stables
537b.plain: Obtaining livery hire or credit at a livery or feed stable without paying or by false pretense, abusing a hired horse or vehicle, or keeping, overusing, or abandoning it to defraud the stable is a misdemeanor.
acts: obtains any livery hire or other accommodation at any livery or feed stable
obtains credit at any such livery or feed stable
abuses the same by beating, goading, overdriving or other willful or malicious conduct
keep the same for a longer period, or take the same to a greater distance than contracted for

537c.title: Unauthorized use of boarded animals or vehicles
537c.plain: A stable keeper or person pasturing stock who rides, drives, or uses an animal or vehicle left in their care, or lets others do so, without the owner's consent is guilty of a misdemeanor.
acts: drive, ride or use

537e.title: Property with removed serial numbers
537e.plain: Knowingly buying, selling, receiving, hiding, or possessing personal property whose serial or identification number has been removed or altered is punishable by up to six months or one year in county jail, or up to three years for computer chips.
acts: buys, sells, receives, disposes of, conceals, or has in his or her possession any personal property

537f.title: Unlabeled rebuilt car batteries
537f.plain: Selling or offering for sale a car battery made with used containers or plates without labeling it "Rebuilt" with the rebuilder's name and address is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail.
acts: selling or offering for sale such a battery in violation of this section

537g.title: Removing NCIC owner identification numbers
537g.plain: Knowingly removing, defacing, covering, altering, or destroying a National Crime Information Center owner identification number on another's property without permission is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail.
acts: removes, defaces, covers, alters or destroys a National Crime Information Center owner identification number from the personal property of another

538.title: Removing or selling mortgaged property
538.plain: After mortgaging property, removing it from the county without the mortgagee's written consent, or selling, destroying, or further encumbering it, to defraud the mortgagee, is theft; no punishment is stated here.
acts: takes, drives, carries away, or otherwise removes or permits the taking, driving, or carrying away, or other removal of the mortgaged property
sells, transfers, slaughters, destroys, or in any manner further encumbers the mortgaged property

538a.title: Signing another's name to a newspaper letter
538a.plain: Signing someone else's name to a letter and sending it to a newspaper, intending the paper to believe that person wrote it, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: signs any letter addressed to a newspaper with the name of a person other than himself and sends such letter to the newspaper, or causes it to be sent to such newspaper

538b.title: Wearing insignia of societies or religious orders
538b.plain: Wearing the badge, garb, or insignia of a secret society, fraternal or religious order, or church without being entitled to, or using it to get aid, with intent to deceive, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: wears the badge, lapel button, rosette, or any part of the garb, robe, habit, or any other recognized and established insignia or apparel of any secret society, or fraternal or religious order or organization, or of any sect, church or religious denomination
uses the same to obtain aid or assistance within this State

538c.title: Theft of advertising services
538c.plain: Attaching or inserting an unauthorized advertisement in a newspaper and redistributing it, or intending to, is the misdemeanor of theft of advertising services; no term is stated here.
acts: attaches or inserts an unauthorized advertisement in a newspaper

538d.title: Impersonating a peace officer
538d.plain: Wearing or using police uniforms, badges, or IDs to fraudulently pose as a law enforcement officer, impersonating one to defraud, or making or selling fake badges is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing, of a law enforcement officer
impersonates a law enforcement officer through or on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a law enforcement officer
wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer
sells a uniform identifying a law enforcement agency, without verifying that the purchaser is an employee of the agency

538e.title: Impersonating a firefighter
538e.plain: Wearing or using fire department uniforms, badges, or IDs to fraudulently pose as a firefighter or fire marshal, making or selling fake badges, or falsely claiming fire authority to sell equipment is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a fire department or the Office of the State Fire Marshal
wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer, or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal
falsely represents, in any manner whatsoever, to any other person that they are a fire marshal, fire inspector or member of a fire department
sells a uniform identifying a firefighting agency or department without verifying that the purchaser is an employee or authorized member of the agency or department

538f.title: Impersonating a utility employee
538f.plain: Presenting oneself to a utility customer to fraudulently pose as a public utility or district employee, or credibly impersonating one to defraud, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail.
acts: presents themselves to a utility or district customer
impersonates an employee of a public utility or district on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means

538g.title: Impersonating a government officer or employee
538g.plain: Wearing or using a public officer's or employee's badge, ID card, or insignia to fraudulently pose as one, impersonating one to defraud, or making or selling fake badges is a misdemeanor; no jail term is stated here.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized badge, photographic identification card, or insignia of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, photographic identification card, or insignia, which falsely purports to be for the use of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee

538h.title: Impersonating search and rescue personnel
538h.plain: Wearing or using search and rescue uniforms or badges to fraudulently pose as a team member or obtain aid or money, or impersonating one to defraud, is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail for badge misuse.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
uses the same to obtain aid, money, or assistance within this state
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

538i.title: Impersonating a first responder during evacuations
538i.plain: Fraudulently posing as a first responder in an area under an evacuation order, or impersonating one online during or within 30 days after an evacuation order to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of a first responder
impersonates a first responder on an internet website, or by other electronic means

538.5.title: Wire fraud to obtain public utility information
538.5.plain: Transmitting communications by wire, radio, or television to obtain a public utility's confidential information, trade secrets, or customer records by false pretenses is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: transmits or causes to be transmitted by means of wire, radio or television communication any words, sounds, writings, signs, signals, or pictures

539.title: False certification of community service
539.plain: Certifying, with intent to defraud, that someone ordered to do community service as a probation condition finished the required hours when they did not is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: certifies that a person ordered by the court to participate in community service as a condition of probation has completed the number of hours of community service prescribed in the court order

548.title: Destroying insured property to defraud insurer
548.plain: Willfully injuring, destroying, hiding, abandoning, or disposing of insured property to defraud the insurer is a felony punishable by two, three, or five years and a fine up to $50,000, plus two years per prior conviction.
acts: injures, destroys, secretes, abandons, or disposes of any property which at the time is insured against loss or damage by theft, or embezzlement, or any casualty

549.title: Referring business for insurance fraud
549.plain: Soliciting, accepting, or referring business knowing or recklessly disregarding that someone intends to commit insurance fraud is punishable by up to one year in county jail or up to three years, a large fine, and restitution.
acts: solicits, accepts, or refers any business to or from any individual or entity

550.title: Insurance fraud
550.plain: Knowingly presenting false insurance or health care claims, staging vehicle collisions, or making false statements to support or oppose insurance claims is punishable by up to five years plus enhancements, fines, and restitution.
acts: present or cause to be presented any false or fraudulent claim for the payment of a loss or injury
present multiple claims for the same loss or injury
cause or participate in a vehicular collision, or any other vehicular accident
present a false or fraudulent claim for the payments of a loss for theft, destruction, damage, or conversion of a motor vehicle
prepare, make, or subscribe any writing
make or cause to be made any false or fraudulent claim for payment of a health care benefit
submit a claim for a health care benefit that was not used by, or on behalf of, the claimant
present multiple claims for payment of the same health care benefit
present for payment any undercharges for health care benefits on behalf of a specific claimant
Present or cause to be presented any written or oral statement as part of, or in support of or opposition to, a claim for payment or other benefit pursuant to an insurance policy
Prepare or make any written or oral statement that is intended to be presented to any insurer or any insurance claimant
Conceal
fail to disclose the occurrence of, an event that affects any person
Prepare or make any written or oral statement, intended to be presented to any insurer or producer for the purpose of obtaining a motor vehicle insurance policy

551.title: Insurance referral kickbacks and deductible waivers
551.plain: Auto repair dealers and contractors who pay insurance agents or adjusters for referrals, or knowingly offer discounts to offset insurance deductibles, commit a public offense punishable by up to three years when over $950.
acts: offer to any insurance agent, broker, or adjuster any fee, commission, profit sharing, or other form of direct or indirect consideration
offer or give any discount intended to offset a deductible required by a policy of insurance

552.title: Posted-property article exceptions for officers and roads
552.plain: Says the posted-property trespass article does not apply to entries by peace officers or other authorized public officers on duty, or to lawful use of an existing public road right of way.

552.1.title: Posted-property article exceptions for labor activity
552.1.plain: Says the posted-property trespass article does not prohibit lawful labor union organizing activity or authorized union investigations of working-condition safety on posted property.

553.title: Posted-property definitions
553.plain: Defines "sign," "posted property," and "posted boundary" for the posted-property trespass article.

554.title: Property that may be posted against trespassing
554.plain: Lists the kinds of utility, oil, gas, water, explosives, railroad, sewer, and quarry property that may be posted against trespassing and loitering.

554.1.title: How property is posted against trespassing
554.1.plain: Sets where and how often signs must be placed to post property described in Section 554 against trespassing and loitering, depending on fencing, size, and type of structure.

555.title: Entering posted property
555.plain: Entering or remaining on posted property without the written permission of the owner, tenant, or occupant is unlawful, and each day is a separate offense; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: enter or remain upon any posted property

555.1.title: Destroying posted-property signs
555.1.plain: Tearing down, defacing, or destroying a sign posted under the posted-property article without authority is unlawful; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: tear down, deface or destroy any sign posted pursuant to this article

555.2.title: Loitering near posted property
555.2.plain: Loitering in the immediate vicinity of posted property is unlawful, though picketing and lawful labor-dispute publicity are allowed; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: loiter in the immediate vicinity of any posted property

555.3.title: Posted-property violations are misdemeanors
555.3.plain: Violating any provision of the posted-property trespass article is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: Violation of any of the provisions of this article

555.4.title: Posted-property article applies statewide
555.4.plain: Makes the posted-property article apply in all counties and cities and bars local ordinances that conflict with it.

555.5.title: Posted-property article severability
555.5.plain: Provides that if any part of the posted-property article is held invalid, the rest remains in effect.

556.title: Advertising signs on public property
556.plain: Placing or keeping advertising signs, pictures, or devices on state, city, or county property without lawful permission is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: place or maintain, or cause to be placed or maintained

556.1.title: Advertising signs on private property
556.1.plain: Placing or keeping advertising signs, pictures, or devices on property where one has no estate or right of possession, without the owner's or possessor's prior consent, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: place or maintain or cause to be placed or maintained upon any property in which he has no estate or right of possession

556.2.title: Exceptions to sign-posting crimes
556.2.plain: Says Sections 556 and 556.1 do not bar legally required or court-ordered notices, notices about the premises where posted, or public highway and street name, direction, or condition signs.

556.3.title: Unlawful signs are a public nuisance
556.3.plain: Declares any sign, picture, advertisement, or device placed on property in violation of Sections 556 and 556.1 to be a public nuisance.

556.4.title: Evidence of who posted a sign
556.4.plain: Allows names, phone numbers, addresses, and other identifying information on a sign or advertisement to be used as evidence, and to create an inference, of who is responsible for posting it.

558.title: Entering Scripps Institution lands
558.plain: Anyone other than University of California officers, employees, students, or licensees is forbidden to enter, trespass on, or interfere with the Scripps Institution of Oceanography lands or adjacent state waters; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: enter upon those lands bordering on the Pacific Ocean in San Diego County
trespass upon the same
interfere with the exclusive possession, occupation, and use thereof by the Regents of the University of California

558.1.title: Punishment for Scripps lands trespass
558.1.plain: Violating Section 558, which bars unauthorized entry onto the Scripps Institution of Oceanography lands, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $600, up to 30 days' imprisonment, or both.
acts: violates any of the provisions of Section 558

560.title: Issuing document of title for goods not received
560.plain: A bailee issuing a document of title, or anyone securing its issue or negotiating it for value, knowing the goods were not actually received or under the bailee's control, faces a felony jail term, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
acts: issues or aids in issuing a document of title
secures the issue by a bailee of a document of title
negotiates or transfers for value a document of title

560.1.title: Issuing receipt with false statement
560.1.plain: A bailee who fraudulently issues, or helps issue, a receipt for goods knowing it contains a false statement is punishable by up to one year of imprisonment, a fine up to $1,000, or both.
acts: issuing a receipt for goods

560.2.title: Delivering goods while document of title outstanding
560.2.plain: A bailee who delivers goods knowing an outstanding, uncanceled negotiable document of title covers them, without first getting that document back, is punishable by up to one year of imprisonment, a fine up to $1,000, or both.
acts: delivers goods out of the possession of such bailee

560.3.title: Negotiating document of title without title
560.3.plain: Depositing goods one does not own, or that carry a security interest, taking a negotiable document of title, and then negotiating it for value to deceive without disclosure is punishable by up to one year, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: deposits goods with a bailee
negotiates for value

560.4.title: Issuing unmarked duplicate document of title
560.4.plain: A bailee who issues a duplicate or additional negotiable document of title, knowing an earlier one is outstanding, without plainly marking it "duplicate" faces a felony jail term, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
acts: issues or aids in issuing a duplicate or additional negotiable document of title for goods

560.5.title: Warehouseman hiding own ownership of goods
560.5.plain: A warehouseman, or its officers, agents, or servants, who knowingly issues a negotiable document of title for goods the warehouseman owns without stating that ownership is punishable by up to one year, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: issues or aids in issuing a negotiable document of title for such goods which does not state such ownership

560.6.title: False receipts for out-of-state warehouse goods
560.6.plain: Knowingly issuing or transferring in California false or unverified receipts for goods in out-of-state warehouses is a misdemeanor punishable by a $50 to $1,000 fine and up to six months in county jail.
acts: issue, sell, pledge, assign, or transfer in this State any receipt, certificate, or other written instrument purporting to be a warehouse receipt
issue, sell, pledge, assign, or transfer in this State any receipt, certificate, or other written instrument for goods, wares, or merchandise claimed to be stored or deposited

issue, sign, sell, pledge, assign, or transfer in this State any receipt, certificate, or other written instrument evidencing, or purporting to evidence, the creation of a security interest in, or sale, or bailment, of any goods

565.title: Misusing branded dairy equipment ($950 or less)
565.plain: An unauthorized person who possesses, uses, or destroys the brand on registered dairy containers, cabinets, or equipment worth $950 or less commits a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: possess or use, or to obliterate or destroy the brand registration upon, containers (including milk cases), cabinets, or other dairy equipment

566.title: Misusing branded dairy equipment (over $950)
566.plain: An unauthorized person who possesses, uses, or destroys the brand on registered dairy containers, cabinets, or equipment worth over $950 commits a felony punishable by a $1,500 fine, a felony jail term, or both.
acts: possess or use, or to obliterate or destroy the brand registration upon, containers (including milk cases), cabinets, or other dairy equipment

570.title: Punishment for unlawful subleasing of vehicles
570.plain: Unlawful subleasing of a motor vehicle, as defined in Section 571, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
acts: unlawful subleasing of a motor vehicle

571.title: Unlawful subleasing of a motor vehicle defined
571.plain: Defines unlawful subleasing of a motor vehicle: a non-party who, for compensation and without the creditor's written consent, transfers or arranges transfer of rights in a vehicle whose contract bars transfer.

572.title: Contract parties not unlawful subleasers
572.plain: Says a transfer, or arranging a transfer, by a party to the vehicle lease, sale, or security contract is not unlawful subleasing, and the chapter does not affect enforcement of those contracts.

573.title: Unlawful subleasing penalties are cumulative
573.plain: Says the chapter's penalties add to other remedies and penalties provided by law, and that an invalid provision does not affect the rest of the chapter.

574.title: Unlawful subleasing definitions
574.plain: Defines terms such as buyer, conditional sale contract, lease contract, motor vehicle, person, security agreement, and seller for the unlawful subleasing chapter.

577.title: Carrier issuing false bill of lading
577.plain: A carrier, vessel master, or transportation company agent who delivers a bill of lading or receipt showing goods were shipped when they were not shipped and under the carrier's control faces a felony jail term, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: delivers any bill of lading, receipt or other voucher

578.title: Warehouseman issuing receipt for goods not received
578.plain: A warehouseman or other depositary who issues a receipt or bill of lading for merchandise not actually received on its premises and under its control faces a felony jail term, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: issues any receipt, bill of lading, or other voucher for any merchandise of any description

579.title: Package contents not matching description
579.plain: Says no one may be convicted under Section 577 or 578 because package contents did not match the description, if the description substantially matched the outside marks, unless the accused knew the marks were untrue.

580.title: Issuing unmarked duplicate receipts
580.plain: A carrier or warehouseman who issues a second or duplicate receipt while an earlier one for the same merchandise is outstanding, without writing "Duplicate" across its face, faces a felony jail term, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: issues any second or duplicate receipt or voucher

581.title: Selling goods covered by own receipt
581.plain: A carrier or warehouseman who sells, hypothecates, or pledges merchandise for which it issued a bill of lading or receipt, without the holder's written consent, faces a felony jail term, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: sells, hypothecates, or pledges any merchandise for which any bill of lading, receipt, or voucher has been issued by him or her

583.title: Exception for sales by legal process
583.plain: Says Section 581 does not apply where the property is demanded or sold by virtue of process of law.

587.title: Malicious damage to railroads
587.plain: Maliciously removing, damaging, or destroying any part of a railroad or its structures, or placing an obstruction on railroad tracks, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: Removes, displaces, injures, or destroys any part of any railroad
Places any obstruction upon the rails or track of any railroad

587.1.title: Moving a locomotive without authorization
587.1.plain: Maliciously moving a locomotive without authorization is a misdemeanor punishable by up to one year in county jail; if it creates a substantial likelihood of injury or death, it may also be a felony.
acts: moves or causes to be moved

587a.title: Tampering with railroad brakes or signals
587a.plain: Tampering or interfering, without the railroad's authorization, with air brakes or other equipment on railroad cars or locomotives, or with switches or signals, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: manipulate or in anywise tamper or interfere with any air brake or other device, appliance or apparatus in or upon any car or locomotive upon such railroad

587b.title: Unauthorized riding on trains
587b.plain: Climbing on, holding onto, or attaching oneself to a locomotive or railroad car without the railroad's authorization is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $50, up to 30 days' imprisonment, or both.
acts: enter into, climb upon, hold to, or in any manner attach himself to any locomotive, locomotive-engine tender, freight or passenger car upon such railroad, or any portion of any train thereon

587c.title: Railroad fare evasion
587c.plain: Fraudulently evading, or attempting to evade, paying one's fare while traveling on a railroad is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $500, up to six months' imprisonment, or both.
acts: evades, or attempts to evade the payment of his fare

588.title: Damaging highways and bridges
588.plain: Negligently, willfully, or maliciously damaging a public highway, bridge, or lawful private way, or letting water flow onto a public highway in a way that tends to damage it or endanger traffic, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: digs up, removes, displaces, breaks down or otherwise injures or destroys any state or other public highway or bridge
sprinkles, drains, diverts or in any manner permits water from any sprinkler, ditch, canal, flume, or reservoir to flow upon or saturate by seepage any public highway

588a.title: Throwing hazardous objects on highways
588a.plain: Throwing or depositing oil, glass, nails, or other substances likely to injure people, animals, or vehicles on a public highway is a misdemeanor; willfully depositing them intending great bodily injury is a felony; no term is stated here.
acts: throws or deposits any oil, glass bottle, glass, nails, tacks, hoops, wire, cans, or any other substance likely to injure any person, animal or vehicle upon any public highway in the State of California
deposits any such substance upon any public highway in the State of California

588b.title: Damaging road barriers and warning signs
588b.plain: Breaking down or removing road barriers placed by highway authorities or their contractors, or destroying road warning signs, notices, directional signs, or warning lights, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: breaks down, removes, injures, or destroys any barrier or obstruction erected or placed in or upon any road or highway
tears down, defaces, removes, or destroys any warnings, notices, or directional signs
extinguishes, removes, injures, or destroys any warning light or lantern, or reflectorized warning or directional sign

590.title: Damaging highway mileposts and guideposts
590.plain: Maliciously removing, destroying, damaging, or defacing a mile post, guide post, or similar marker on or near a highway, or its inscription, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: removes, destroys, injures, breaks or defaces any mile post, board or stone, or guide post erected on or near any highway, or any inscription thereon

590a.title: Informer's share of milepost fines
590a.plain: Half of all fines collected for damaging highway mileposts and guideposts under Section 590 go to the informer who first causes a complaint to be filed.

591.title: Damaging telephone, cable, or power lines
591.plain: Unlawfully and maliciously cutting, removing, or obstructing telegraph, telephone, cable television, or electric lines, or making an unauthorized connection to an electric line, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term of up to three years.
acts: takes down, removes, injures, disconnects, cuts, or obstructs a line of telegraph, telephone, or cable television, or any line used to conduct electricity
severs any wire thereof
makes an unauthorized connection with any line, other than a telegraph, telephone, or cable television line, used to conduct electricity

591.5.title: Disabling a phone to block emergency calls
591.5.plain: Unlawfully and maliciously removing, damaging, or obstructing the use of a wireless communication device to stop someone from calling for help or reporting a crime is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: removes, injures, destroys, damages, or obstructs the use of any wireless communication device

592.title: Stealing water from canals or reservoirs
592.plain: Taking water from a canal, ditch, flume, or reservoir without the owner's authority and with intent to defraud is a misdemeanor; if the water is worth over $950 or the person has a prior conviction, it can bring county jail or state prison.
acts: take water from any canal, ditch, flume, or reservoir

593.title: Damaging electric power lines
593.plain: Unlawfully and maliciously taking down, damaging, or interfering with an authorized electric power line or its parts, wires, or current is punishable by a felony jail term, a fine up to $1,000, or up to one year in county jail.
acts: takes down, removes, injures, interferes with, or obstructs any line erected or maintained by proper authority for the purpose of transmitting electricity for light, heat, or power
severs or in any way interferes with any wire, cable, or current thereof

593a.title: Spiking trees and logs
593a.plain: Maliciously driving metal, ceramic, or other hard objects into trees or logs meant for harvest or lumber, which can injure saws, is a felony; causing bodily injury adds a consecutive three-year prison term.
acts: drives or places, in any tree, saw-log, shingle-bolt, or other wood, any iron, steel, ceramic, or other substance sufficiently hard to injure saws

593b.title: Climbing electric transmission towers
593b.plain: Climbing an electric transmission or distribution pole or tower without written permission of its owner or operator is a misdemeanor, except for utility employees on duty; no term is stated here.
acts: climb upon any pole, tower or other structure which is a part of such line or system

593c.title: Damaging gas or hazardous liquid pipelines
593c.plain: Willfully and maliciously breaking, obstructing, or interfering with a gas or hazardous liquid pipeline, its equipment, or its valves is a felony; no term is stated here.
acts: breaks, digs up, obstructs, interferes with, removes or injures any pipe or main or hazardous liquid pipeline
shuts off, removes, obstructs, injures, or in any way interferes with any valve or fitting installed on, connected to, or operated in connection with any such main or pipeline

593d.title: Cable and video service theft
593d.plain: Making unauthorized connections or using devices to get cable, satellite, or similar video services without authorization, or making or selling descrambling devices, is a crime; dealing in 10 or more devices can bring county jail or state prison and fines up to $250,000.
acts: makes or maintains an unauthorized connection or connections
purchases, possesses, attaches, causes to be attached, assists others in attaching, or maintains the attachment of any unauthorized device or devices
makes or maintains any modification or alteration to any device installed with the authorization of a multichannel video or information services provider
makes or maintains any modifications or alterations to an access device that authorizes services
obtains an unauthorized access device and uses the modified, altered, or unauthorized access device to obtain services from a multichannel video or information services provider
manufactures, assembles, modifies, imports into this state, distributes, sells, offers to sell, advertises for sale, or possesses for any of these purposes, any device or kit for a device
attaches, causes to be attached, assists others in attaching, or maintains any attachment to, any cable, wire, or other component of a multichannel video or information services provider’s system

593e.title: Subscription television signal theft
593e.plain: Making unauthorized connections or attaching devices to get subscription television without authorization, or making or selling decoding devices for it, is a misdemeanor; repeat device dealing brings up to one year in county jail and a $20,000 fine.
acts: makes or maintains an unauthorized connection or connections

purchases, possesses, attaches, causes to be attached, assists others in or maintains the attachment of any unauthorized device or devices to a television set or to other equipment designed to receive a television broadcast or transmission
makes or maintains any modification or alteration to any device installed with the authorization of a subscription television system

manufactures, imports into this state, assembles, distributes, sells, offers to sell, possesses, advertises for sale, or otherwise provides any device, any plan, or any kit for a device or for a printed circuit

593f.title: Selling devices to decode MDS or ITFS broadcasts
593f.plain: Making, distributing, or selling for profit devices, plans, or kits to decode unauthorized Multi-point Distribution Service or Instructional Television Fixed Service broadcasts is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $2,500, up to 90 days in county jail, or both.
acts: manufactures, distributes, or sells any device or plan or kit for a device, or printed circuit containing circuitry for decoding or addressing

593g.title: Possessing tree-spiking materials
593g.plain: Possessing iron, steel, ceramic, or other hard substances that can damage saws or wood processing equipment, intending to use them to spike trees or logs in violation of Section 593a, is punishable by up to one year in county jail.
acts: possesses any iron, steel, ceramic, or other substance sufficiently hard to injure saws or wood manufacturing or processing equipment
